title.zh: 卷一百〇五 載記第五 石勒下
title.en: Volume 105 Records 5: Shi Le Part Two
title.raw: 卷一百〇五 載記第五 石勒下 Volume 105 Records 5: Shi Le Part Two

sentences.zh: 石勒

translations.literal: The chapter heading gives the name Shi Le.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le.

translations.literal: The rubric reads “(Part Two).”
translations.idiomatic: Part Two.

sentences.zh: 太興二年，勒偽稱趙王，赦殊死已下，均百姓田租之半，賜孝悌力田死義之孤帛各有差，孤老鰥寡谷人三石，大酺七日。

translations.literal: In the second year of the Taixing era, Le falsely assumed the title King of Zhao, amnestied crimes less than capital, halved the commoners’ land tax, bestowed silk in graded amounts to orphans distinguished for filial piety, diligence in farming, or a parent’s death in loyal service, gave three shi of grain per person to orphans, the aged, widowers, and widows, and ordered a seven-day general feast.
translations.idiomatic: In 319, the second year of Taixing, Shi Le took the title of King of Zhao. He proclaimed an amnesty stopping short of capital offenses, cut the land levy for ordinary households by half, distributed graded silk awards to orphans noted for filial devotion, tireless farming, or parents lost in loyal service, allotted three shi of grain each to the isolated elderly and bereft, and declared seven days of public feasting.

sentences.zh: 依春秋列國、漢初侯王每世稱元，改稱趙王元年。

translations.literal: Following the Spring and Autumn practice of feudal states and the early Han marquises and kings, who in each reign took a fresh “first year,” he changed the reckoning to “first year of the King of Zhao.”
translations.idiomatic: He followed the old convention—seen in the Spring and Autumn states and early Han fiefs—where each ruler began a new year count, and renamed the calendar to the first year of his Zhao kingship.

sentences.zh: 始建社稷，立宗廟，營東西宮。

translations.literal: He first founded the altars of soil and grain, set up the ancestral temple, and constructed eastern and western palaces.
translations.idiomatic: He established the state altars of soil and grain, dedicated the imperial ancestral shrine, and built paired eastern and western palace halls.

sentences.zh: 署從事中郎裴憲、參軍傅暢、杜嘏並領經學祭酒，參軍續咸、庾景為律學祭酒，任播、崔濬為史學祭酒。

translations.literal: He assigned Senior Administrators Pei Xian and Fu Chang and Adjutant Du Jia jointly to head the libationer for classical studies; Adjutants Xu Xian and Yu Jing as libationers for legal studies; and Ren Bo and Cui Jun as libationers for historical studies.
translations.idiomatic: He put Pei Xian, Fu Chang, and Du Jia—in posts from senior administrator down to adjutant—in charge of the academy of the Classics; named the adjutants Xu Xian and Yu Jing to oversee legal scholarship; and charged Ren Bo and Cui Jun with the school of history.

sentences.zh: 中壘支雄、遊擊王陽並領門臣祭酒，專明胡人辭訟，以張離、張良、劉群、劉謨等為門生主書，司典胡人出內，重其禁法，不得侮易衣冠華族。

translations.literal: Central Rampart Zhi Xiong and Mobile Corps commander Wang Yang together headed the libationer for gate attendants, exclusively clarifying lawsuits among the Hu; Zhang Li, Zhang Liang, Liu Qun, Liu Mo, and others were made chief clerks of the disciples of the gate, superintending Hu persons’ exits and entries, tightening prohibitions so that they might not insult or slight cap-and-gown Chinese clans.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Xiong of the central rampart guard and Wang Yang, who led light raiders, were both given the “libationer for gate retainers” portfolio to hear only Hu people’s legal pleas; Zhang Li, Zhang Liang, Liu Qun, Liu Mo, and the like became registrar-scribes for those retainers, controlling Hu movement in and out of court under strict rules meant to keep them from lording it over genteel Han families.

sentences.zh: 號胡為國人。

translations.literal: He styled the Hu as “countrymen.”
translations.idiomatic: He officially rebranded the Hu as guoren, “people of the state.”

sentences.zh: 遣使循行州郡，勸課農桑。

translations.literal: He sent agents to tour the provinces and commanderies, exhorting and inspecting farming and sericulture.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched inspectors through the provinces to urge tillage and mulberry-raising.

sentences.zh: 加張賓大執法，專總朝政，位冠僚首。

translations.literal: Zhang Bin was promoted to grand judicial overseer, placed solely in charge of court government, and ranked above all other officials.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Bin was elevated to chief law officer with sweeping authority over administration, outranking the rest of the bureaucracy.

sentences.zh: 署石季龍為單于元輔、都督禁衛諸軍事，署前將軍李寒領司兵勳，教國子擊刺戰射之法。

translations.literal: He appointed Shi Tigun (Hu) as plenary assistant to the Chanyu and supervisor of all affairs of the palace guards; Adjutant General Li Han was put in charge of the bureau of military merit and instructed the sons of the state in thrusting, stabbing, combat, and archery.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu was named senior aide to the Chanyu and given overall command of the household guards; General of the Van Li Han headed military evaluations and drilled the cadet sons of the elite in close combat and mounted shooting.

sentences.zh: 命記室佐明楷、程機撰《上党國記》，中大夫傅彪、賈蒲、江軌撰《大將軍起居注》，參軍石泰、石同、石謙、孔隆撰《大單于志》。

translations.literal: He ordered secretaries Ming Kai and Cheng Ji to compile the State Chronicle of Shangdang; palace gentlemen Fu Biao, Jia Pu, and Jiang Gui to compile the Daily Records of the Grand General; and adjutants Shi Tai, Shi Tong, Shi Qian, and Kong Long to compile the Treatise of the Grand Chanyu.
translations.idiomatic: He set Ming Kai and Cheng Ji to writing the Shangdang state annals; Fu Biao, Jia Pu, and Jiang Gui to keep the grand general’s court diary; and Shi Tai, Shi Tong, Shi Qian, and Kong Long to draft a record of the grand Chanyu’s affairs.

sentences.zh: 自是朝會常以天子禮樂饗其群下，威儀冠冕從容可觀矣。

translations.literal: From this time court gatherings regularly used the Son of Heaven’s ritual music to feast his subordinates, and the majesty of caps and gowns became composed and worth viewing.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth his levees borrowed imperial ritual and music to regale his ministers, and the spectacle of court dress grew as stately as any emperor’s.

sentences.zh: 群臣議請論功，勒曰：「自孤起軍，十六年於茲矣。

translations.literal: The ministers deliberated and asked to assess merit; Le said, “Since I raised an army, sixteen years have passed to this day.
translations.idiomatic: His officials debated how to reward past service; Shi Le said, “It has been sixteen years since I first took the field.

sentences.zh: 文武將士從孤征伐者，莫不蒙犯矢石，備嘗艱阻，其在葛陂之役，厥功尤著，宜為賞之先也。

translations.literal: Among civil and military officers and soldiers who followed me on campaign, none failed to brave arrows and stones and taste every hardship; in the affair of Gebei their merit was especially conspicuous, and they ought to be first in receiving rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Every commander and trooper who marched with me has faced missile fire and every sort of peril; those who fought at Gebei deserve pride of place in any grant of honors.

sentences.zh: 若身見存，爵封輕重隨功位為差，死事之孤，賞加一等，庶足以尉答存亡，申孤之心也。

translations.literal: If they still live, let noble rank and fiefs vary by merit and station; for orphans of those who died in service, raise the reward one grade—perhaps that may suffice to comfort the living and dead and express what is in my heart.”
translations.idiomatic: For survivors, match titles and fiefs to what they earned; for children of the fallen, add one step to the bounty—so I may answer both the quick and the dead and show what I owe them.”

sentences.zh: 」又下書禁國人不聽報嫂及在喪婚娶，其燒葬令如本俗。

translations.literal: ” He further issued documents forbidding countrymen to take a brother’s widow in marriage or to marry while in mourning, and ordered cremation burials to follow their native customs.
translations.idiomatic: ” He also banned levirate remarriage and weddings during mourning for his Hu subjects, while letting funeral pyres follow steppe custom.

sentences.zh: 孔萇攻邵續別營十一，皆下之。

translations.literal: Kong Chang attacked eleven detached camps of Shao Xu and took them all.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Chang stormed eleven of Shao Xu’s outlying stockades and reduced each one.

sentences.zh: 續尋為石季龍所獲，送于襄國。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Xu was captured by Shi Tigun (Hu) and sent to Xiangguo.
translations.idiomatic: Shao Xu was soon seized by Shi Hu and marched to the capital at Xiangguo.

sentences.zh: 劉曜將尹安、宋始據洛陽，降於勒。

translations.literal: Liu Yao’s generals Yin An and Song Shi held Luoyang and surrendered to Le.
translations.idiomatic: Yin An and Song Shi, holding Luoyang for Liu Yao, came over to Shi Le.

sentences.zh: 晉徐州刺史蔡豹敗徐龕于檀丘，龕遣使詣勒，陳討豹之計。

translations.literal: Jin’s Inspector of Xuzhou, Cai Bao, defeated Xu Kan at Tanqiu; Kan sent envoys to Le laying out a plan to strike Bao.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Bao, Jin governor of Xuzhou, routed Xu Kan near Tanqiu, whereupon Kan dispatched messengers to Shi Le with a scheme for destroying Cai Bao.

sentences.zh: 勒遣將王步都為龕前鋒，使張敬率騎繼之。

translations.literal: Le sent the general Wang Budu as Kan’s vanguard and ordered Zhang Jing to follow with cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le gave Wang Budu command of Xu Kan’s van and had Zhang Jing bring up the horse behind him.

sentences.zh: 敬達東平，龕疑敬之襲已也，斬步都等三百餘人，復降于晉。

translations.literal: When Jing reached Dongping, Kan suspected Jing meant to attack him, beheaded Budu and more than three hundred others, and again submitted to Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching Dongping, Zhang Jing alarmed Xu Kan, who feared a stab in the back, executed Wang Budu and over three hundred men, and reverted to Jin allegiance.

sentences.zh: 勒大怒，命張敬據其襟要以守之。

translations.literal: Le was greatly angered and ordered Zhang Jing to seize his strategic points and hold them.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le, furious, told Zhang Jing to occupy Xu Kan’s chokepoints and bottle him up.

sentences.zh: 大雨霖，中山、常山尤甚，滹沲汛溢，沖陷山谷，巨松僵拔，浮於滹沲，東至渤海，原隰間皆如山積。

translations.literal: Heavy rains fell in long spells; Zhongshan and Changshan were especially hard hit, the Hutuo swelled and overflowed, washing out valleys, snapping and uprooting great pines that floated on the Hutuo east to the Bohai Sea, until upland and marsh alike were piled like mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Relentless downpours soaked Hebei; around Zhongshan and Changshan the Hutuo burst its banks, tearing gullies loose and tearing up ancient pines that rode the flood east toward the Bohai until driftwood lay in hills across plain and fen.

sentences.zh: 孔萇攻陷文鴦十餘營，萇不設備，鴦夜擊之，大敗而歸。

translations.literal: Kong Chang stormed more than ten camps of Wen Yang; Chang took no precautions, and Yang struck by night, routing him so that he fled home in defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Chang overran a dozen of Wen Yang’s camps but grew careless; Wen Yang counterattacked at night and sent him fleeing in rout.

sentences.zh: 勒始制軒懸之樂，八佾之舞，為金根大輅，黃屋左纛，天子車旗，禮樂備矣。

translations.literal: Le first instituted the suspended bells and chimes, the eight rows of dancers, built a gold-rooted great chariot, yellow canopy and left-side yak-tail banner—the carriages and banners of the Son of Heaven—so ritual and music were complete.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le introduced imperial-grade music and the eight-row dance, commissioned the gilded state coach with yellow awning and banner of rank, and copied the full panoply of regalia befitting a Son of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 使石季龍率步騎四萬討徐龕，龕遣長史劉霄詣勒乞降，送妻子為質，納之。

translations.literal: He had Shi Tigun lead forty thousand foot and horse to punish Xu Kan; Kan sent his chief clerk Liu Xiao to Le to beg surrender, sending wife and children as hostages, and Le accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu marched forty thousand mixed troops against Xu Kan, who dispatched chief clerk Liu Xiao to sue for peace, offering his family as hostages; Shi Le accepted the terms.

sentences.zh: 時蔡豹屯於譙城，季龍攻豹，豹夜遁，季龍引軍城封丘而旋。

translations.literal: At the time Cai Bao was encamped at Qiao city; Tigun attacked Bao, Bao fled by night, and Tigun led the army to wall Fengqiu and then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: While Cai Bao held Qiao, Shi Hu struck his camp; Bao slipped away under cover of dark, and Shi Hu fortified Fengqiu before marching home.

sentences.zh: 徙朝臣掾屬已上士族者三百戶于襄國崇仁裏，置公族大夫以領之。

translations.literal: He moved three hundred households of court officials and clerks upward who were of genteel clans to Chongren ward in Xiangguo, setting up noble-clan grandees to supervise them.
translations.idiomatic: He resettled three hundred elite-official families into Chongren Lane at Xiangguo and appointed “noble-clan” overseers for them.

sentences.zh: 勒宮殿及諸門始就，制法令甚嚴，諱胡尤峻。

translations.literal: Le’s palaces and the various gates were newly completed; he made laws and orders very strict, and taboos on the word “Hu” were especially harsh.
translations.idiomatic: With his palaces and gates finished, Shi Le tightened the legal code and cracked down hardest on any mention of “Hu.”

sentences.zh: 有醉胡乘馬突入止車門，勒大怒，謂宮門小執法馮翥曰：「夫人君為令，尚望威行天下，況宮闕之間乎！

translations.literal: A drunken Hu rode a horse bursting through the chariot-halting gate; Le was greatly angered and said to the minor gate law officer Feng Xu, “When a lord of men makes orders, he still hopes awe will extend through the world—how much more within palace gates!
translations.idiomatic: A drunken Hu rider crashed the coach-stop gate; Shi Le rounded on minor gate magistrate Feng Xu: “If a ruler’s word is to awe the realm, what of the palace itself!

sentences.zh: 向馳馬入門為是何人，而不彈白邪？

translations.literal: Just now one who galloped a horse through the gate—what manner of person was he, that you did not impeach and report?”
translations.idiomatic: Someone just charged the gate on horseback—who was he, and why was he not reported?”

sentences.zh: 」翥惶懼忘諱，對曰：「向有醉胡乘馬馳入，甚呵禦之，而不可與語。

translations.literal: ” Xu, frightened, forgot the taboo and replied, “Just now there was a drunken Hu who rode a horse galloping in; I shouted harshly to restrain him, but could not reason with him.
translations.idiomatic: ” Panicked, Feng Xu slipped and said “Hu”: “A drunk Hu burst through; I yelled at him to stop, but he would not listen.”

sentences.zh: 」勒笑曰：「胡人正自難與言。

translations.literal: ” Le laughed and said, “Hu people are indeed hard to talk with.
translations.idiomatic: ” Shi Le laughed: “You really cannot argue with a Hu in his cups.

sentences.zh: 」恕而不罪。

translations.literal: ” He forgave and did not punish.
translations.idiomatic: ” And he let the matter drop.

sentences.zh: 使石季龍擊托候部掘咄哪於岍北，大破之，俘獲牛馬二十餘萬。

translations.literal: He had Shi Tigun strike the Tuohou tribe’s Judunuo band north of the Qian range, crushing them and capturing prisoners and cattle and horses over two hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu smashed the Tuohou clansmen led by Judunuo beyond the Qian hills, taking more than two hundred thousand captives and animals.

sentences.zh: 勒清定五品，以張賓領選。

translations.literal: Le clarified and fixed the five grades, with Zhang Bin heading selection.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le regularized the five-rank ladder and put Zhang Bin in charge of appointments.

sentences.zh: 復續定九品。

translations.literal: He again continued and fixed the nine grades.
translations.idiomatic: He extended the work to the full nine-grade system.

sentences.zh: 署張班為左執法郎，孟卓為右執法郎，典定士族，副選舉之任。

translations.literal: He appointed Zhang Ban as left law officer and Meng Zhuo as right law officer, to codify genteel clans and assist the duty of selection.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ban and Meng Zhuo became left and right law officers charged with fixing the roster of great families and backing Zhang Bin’s personnel office.

sentences.zh: 今群僚及州郡歲各舉秀才、至孝、廉清、賢良、直言、武勇之士各一人。

translations.literal: “Now let the host of officials and each province and commandery annually recommend one man each among accomplished scholars, supreme filial sons, incorrupt and pure, worthy and good, outspoken, and martially brave.”
translations.idiomatic: He ordered every yamen and locality to nominate yearly one candidate apiece from the categories of cultivated talent, exemplary filial piety, clean integrity, worthiness, blunt counsel, and martial valor.

sentences.zh: 置署都部從事各一部一州，秩二千石，職准丞相司直。

translations.literal: He established capital-section investigators, one section per province, at salary grade two thousand shi, duties modeled on the chancellor’s rectifier.
translations.idiomatic: Each province gained an investigator-general at two-thousand-shi rank, patterned on the Han chancellor’s inspector.

sentences.zh: 勒下令曰：「去年水出巨材，所在山積，將皇天欲孤繕修宮宇也！

translations.literal: Le issued an order saying, “Last year floodwaters brought forth huge timbers, piled like mountains wherever they lay—perhaps Heaven wishes me to repair palace buildings!
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le proclaimed: “Last year’s floods washed down giant logs in drifts—is this Heaven telling me to finish my halls?

sentences.zh: 其擬洛陽之太極起建德殿。

translations.literal: Let them model Luoyang’s Taiji Hall and raise the Jiande Palace.”
translations.idiomatic: Take Luoyang’s Taiji Hall as the model and raise Jiande Palace.”

sentences.zh: 」遣從事中郎任汪帥使工匠五千采木以供之。

translations.literal: ” He sent Adjutant Ren Wang to lead five thousand craftsmen to gather timber to supply it.
translations.idiomatic: ” He dispatched Ren Wang with five thousand woodcutters to feed the project.

sentences.zh: 黎陽人陳武妻一產三男一女，武攜其妻子詣襄國上書自陳。

translations.literal: A Liyang man, Chen Wu, had a wife who in one birth bore three boys and a girl; Wu brought wife and children to Xiangguo and submitted a memorial stating the fact.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Wu of Liyang reported that his wife had delivered quadruplets—three sons and a daughter—and brought the whole family to Xiangguo to file notice.

sentences.zh: 勒下書以為二儀諧暢，和氣所致，賜其乳婢一口，谷一百石，雜彩四十匹。

translations.literal: Le issued documents holding it harmony of the Two Principles and a product of harmonious qi, bestowing one wet-nurse slave, one hundred shi of grain, and forty bolts of assorted silks.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le treated it as cosmic concord and sent a nursemaid, a hundred shi of grain, and forty rolls of colored silk.

sentences.zh: 石季龍攻段匹磾於厭次。

translations.literal: Shi Tigun attacked Duan Pidi at Yanci.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu besieged Duan Pidi in Yanci.

sentences.zh: 孔萇討匹磾部內諸城，陷之。

translations.literal: Kong Chang campaigned against the cities within Pidi’s territory and captured them.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Chang rolled up the towns still loyal to Duan Pidi.

sentences.zh: 匹磾勢窮，乃率其臣下輿櫬出降。

translations.literal: Pidi’s strength was exhausted; then he led his ministers and subordinates with coffin-carts and came out to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Cornered, Duan Pidi emerged with his court bearing their own biers in token of submission.

sentences.zh: 季龍送之襄國，勒署匹磾為冠軍將軍，以其其弟文鴦、亞將衛麟為左右中郎將，皆金章紫綬。

translations.literal: Tigun sent him to Xiangguo; Le appointed Pidi General Who Smashes the Caitiffs, and his younger brother Wen Yang and lieutenant-general Wei Lin as left and right leaders of court gentlemen—all with gold seals and purple ribbons.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu escorted him to Xiangguo, where Shi Le named him champion general and made his brother Wen Yang and adjutant Wei Lin left and right leaders of court gentlemen, each with gold seal and purple ribbon.

sentences.zh: 散諸流人三萬餘戶，復其本業，置守宰以撫之，於是冀、並、幽州、遼西巴西諸屯結皆陷於勒。

translations.literal: He dispersed the various displaced persons, over thirty thousand households, restored them to their original occupations, set up guards and magistrates to soothe them, whereupon the fortified settlements of Ji, Bing, Youzhou, Liaoxi, and Baxi all fell to Le.
translations.idiomatic: He repatriated more than thirty thousand refugee households, reinstalled local officials to settle them, and thereby brought the fortified camps of Ji, Bing, You, western Liaoxi, and Baxi under his control.

sentences.zh: 時晉征北將軍祖逖據譙，將平中原。

translations.literal: At the time Jin’s General Who Conquers the North, Zu Ti, held Qiao, intending to pacify the Central Plain.
translations.idiomatic: Jin’s northern-expedition commander Zu Ti held Qiao, aiming to reconquer the heartland.

sentences.zh: 逖善於撫納，自河以南多背勒歸順。

translations.literal: Ti was skilled at comforting and accepting, and south of the Yellow River many turned their backs on Le and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: South of the Yellow River his conciliatory rule drew many towns away from Shi Le.

sentences.zh: 勒憚之，不敢為寇，乃下書曰：「祖逖屢為邊患。

translations.literal: Le feared him and did not dare raid; then he issued documents saying, “Zu Ti repeatedly has been a border trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le avoided provoking him and announced: “Zu Ti has become a constant frontier threat.

sentences.zh: 逖，北州士望也，儻有首丘之思。

translations.literal: Ti is a man of northern provinces’ gentry repute; perhaps he cherishes thoughts of returning to his mound.”
translations.idiomatic: He is the north’s most respected gentleman; perhaps he longs to tend his ancestors’ graves.”

sentences.zh: 其下幽州，修祖氏墳墓，為置守塚二家。

translations.literal: Let an order go down to Youzhou to repair the Zu clan tombs and assign two households to guard the mounds.”
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Youzhou to refurbish the Zu family cemetery and post two grave-keeping households.

sentences.zh: 冀逖如趙他感恩，輟其寇暴。

translations.literal: He hoped Ti might, like Zhao Tuo, feel gratitude and cease his raiding violence.
translations.idiomatic: He hoped Zu Ti might respond as Zhao Tuo once did—with gratitude—and call off his raids.

sentences.zh: 」逖聞之甚悅，遣參軍王愉使於勒，贈以方物，修結和好。

translations.literal: ” When Ti heard this he was very pleased, sent his adjutant Wang Yu as envoy to Le, presented local products, and cultivated friendly relations.
translations.idiomatic: ” Zu Ti, delighted, sent adjutant Wang Yu with gifts to seal a détente.

sentences.zh: 勒厚賓其使，遣左常侍董樹報聘，以馬百匹、金五十斤答之。

translations.literal: Le richly entertained his envoy, sent Left Permanent Attendant Dong Shu on a return mission, and answered with one hundred horses and fifty jin of gold.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le lavished gifts on the envoy and returned the courtesy through Dong Shu with a hundred horses and fifty jin of gold.

sentences.zh: 自是兗豫乂安，人得休息矣。

translations.literal: From this Yan and Yu were again peaceful and people obtained rest.
translations.idiomatic: Yan and Yu provinces thereafter knew a respite from war.

sentences.zh: 從事中郎劉奧坐營建德殿井木斜縮，斬於殿中。

translations.literal: Adjutant Liu Ao was executed in the hall for the Jiande Palace well timber’s warping and shrinkage.
translations.idiomatic: Adjutant Liu Ao was beheaded in court when support timbers for Jiande Palace warped.

sentences.zh: 勒悔之，贈太常。

translations.literal: Le regretted it and posthumously awarded him Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le regretted the deed and posthumously named him minister of rituals.

sentences.zh: 建德校尉王和掘得員石，銘曰：「律權石，重四鈞，同律度量衡，有新氏造。

translations.literal: Jiande commandant Wang He dug up a round stone whose inscription read, “Legal weight stone, weight four jun, same as the pitch-pipes, measures, and balances—made by the Xin house.”
translations.idiomatic: Wang He, a Jiande garrison officer, unearthed a carved round weight inscribed as a four-jun statutory measure from Wang Mang’s Xin dynasty.

sentences.zh: 」議者未詳，或以為瑞。

translations.literal: ” Discussers did not understand the details; some thought it an auspicious portent.
translations.idiomatic: ” Court scholars could not parse it; some hailed it as an omen.

sentences.zh: 參軍續咸曰：「王莽時物也。

translations.literal: Adjutant Xu Xian said, “It is a thing from Wang Mang’s time.”
translations.idiomatic: Xu Xian said flatly, “That is Wang Mang’s hardware.”

sentences.zh: 」其時兵亂之後，典度堙滅，遂命下禮官為准程定式。

translations.literal: ” At that time, after the military chaos, canonical measures had been buried and lost, so he ordered the inferior ritual officials to set models and fixed patterns.
translations.idiomatic: ” With old standards lost in the wars, he told the ritual office to codify new benchmarks.

sentences.zh: 又得一鼎，容四升，中有大錢三十文，曰：「百當千，千當萬。

translations.literal: Again they obtained a tripod holding four sheng, inside which were thirty large cash reading, “A hundred counts as a thousand, a thousand as ten thousand.”
translations.idiomatic: Another find was a four-sheng cauldron holding thirty large coins inscribed “hundred equals thousand, thousand equals myriad.”

sentences.zh: 」鼎銘十三字，篆書不可曉，藏之於永豐倉。

translations.literal: ” The tripod inscription was thirteen characters in seal script, unintelligible, and it was stored in the Ever-Abundant granary.
translations.idiomatic: ” Its thirteen seal characters could not be read, so the piece went into the Yongfeng treasury.

sentences.zh: 因此令公私行錢，而人情不樂，乃出公絹市錢，限中絹匹一千二百，下絹八百。

translations.literal: On this basis he ordered public and private circulation of cash, but popular feeling was unhappy, so he issued official silk to buy coin, fixing upper-grade silk at twelve hundred per bolt and lower-grade at eight hundred.
translations.idiomatic: He then pushed coinage on a reluctant populace, offering to buy cash with state silk at twelve hundred cash per bolt of medium grade and eight hundred for lower grade.

sentences.zh: 然百姓私買中絹四千，下絹二千，巧利者賤買私錢，貴賣於官，坐死者十數人，而錢終不行。

translations.literal: Yet commoners privately bought medium silk at four thousand and lower at two thousand; the crafty profited by cheaply buying private coin and dearly selling to the office—more than ten persons were sentenced to death for it, yet coin in the end did not circulate.
translations.idiomatic: Speculators undercut the official rates, bought private cash cheap, resold dear to the mint, and a dozen people died on the scaffold—yet the currency reform still failed.

sentences.zh: 勒徙洛陽銅馬、翁仲二于襄國，列之永豐門。

translations.literal: Le moved Luoyang’s bronze horses and two stone giant figures to Xiangguo and arrayed them at Ever-Abundant Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He hauled Luoyang’s bronze horses and paired stone colossi to Xiangguo and set them before Yongfeng Gate.

sentences.zh: 祖逖牙門童建害新蔡內史周密，遣使降於勒。

translations.literal: Zu Ti’s camp-gate officer Tong Jian killed Xincai interior secretary Zhou Mi and sent envoys to surrender to Le.
translations.idiomatic: Tong Jian, a gate captain under Zu Ti, murdered interior secretary Zhou Mi of Xincai and offered himself to Shi Le.

sentences.zh: 勒斬之，送首于祖逖，曰：「天下之惡一也。

translations.literal: Le beheaded him, sent the head to Zu Ti, and said, “Evil in the world is one.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le executed him and returned the head to Zu Ti with the message: “Villainy is the same everywhere.

sentences.zh: 叛臣逃吏，吾之深仇，將軍之惡，猶吾惡也。

translations.literal: Rebel ministers and fugitive clerks are my deepest hatred; what the general hates is as what I hate.”
translations.idiomatic: A traitor or runaway clerk is my bitter enemy; what offends you offends me.”

sentences.zh: 」逖遣使報謝。

translations.literal: ” Ti sent envoys in return to thank him.
translations.idiomatic: ” Zu Ti sent thanks in reply.

sentences.zh: 自是兗豫間壘壁叛者，逖皆不納，二州之人率多兩屬矣。

translations.literal: From this, among stockade rebels between Yan and Yu, Ti accepted none, and the people of the two provinces mostly had dual allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: After that Zu Ti refused every turncoat from the border forts, and folk in Yan and Yu commonly owed both sides allegiance.

sentences.zh: 勒令武鄉耆舊赴襄國。

translations.literal: Le ordered the elders of Wuxiang to come to Xiangguo.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned Wuxiang’s leading clansmen to Xiangguo.

sentences.zh: 既至，勒親與鄉老齒坐歡飲，語及平生。

translations.literal: When they arrived, Le personally sat with the village elders by age rank, drank merrily, and spoke of their whole lives.
translations.idiomatic: There he sat among them by seniority, drank freely, and reminisced about old times.

sentences.zh: 初，勒與李陽鄰居，歲常爭麻池，迭相驅擊。

translations.literal: Earlier, Le had been neighbor to Li Yang and yearly they often quarreled over a hemp pond, repeatedly driving and striking each other.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he had feuded yearly with neighbor Li Yang over a hemp-soaking pool, trading blows.

sentences.zh: 至是，謂父老曰：「李陽，壯士也，何以不來？

translations.literal: At this point he said to the fathers of the district, “Li Yang is a stalwart man—why does he not come?
translations.idiomatic: Now he asked the elders, “Where is Li Yang, that brave fellow?

sentences.zh: 漚麻是布衣之恨，孤方崇信于天下，寧讎匹夫乎！

translations.literal: Soaking hemp was a commoner’s grudge; I am just now extending trust through the world—would I begrudge a mere commoner?”
translations.idiomatic: A peasant quarrel over soaking hemp is nothing now that I rule the realm—would I nurse a grudge against a villager?”

sentences.zh: 」乃使召陽。

translations.literal: ” Then he had Yang summoned.
translations.idiomatic: ” He had Li Yang fetched.

sentences.zh: 既至，勒與酣謔，引陽臂笑曰：「孤往日厭卿老拳，卿亦飽孤毒手。

translations.literal: When he arrived, Le drank and jested tipsily with him, pulled Yang’s arm and laughed, saying, “In former days I tired of your old fists, and you also had your fill of my vicious hands.”
translations.idiomatic: When Li Yang arrived, Shi Le seized his arm in drunken jest: “I used to dread your famous right hook; you tasted plenty of my knuckles too.”

sentences.zh: 」因賜甲第一區，拜參軍都尉。

translations.literal: ” Thereupon he bestowed one mansion and appointed him adjutant commandant.
translations.idiomatic: ” He then granted him a townhouse and a staff appointment.

sentences.zh: 令曰：「武鄉，吾之豐沛，萬歲之後，魂靈當歸之，其復之三世。

translations.literal: An order said, “Wuxiang is my Feng and Pei; after ten thousand years my soul-spirit ought to return there—exempt it for three generations.”
translations.idiomatic: He decreed Wuxiang his spiritual home like Gaozu’s Feng and Pei, exempted its taxes for three generations, and vowed his ghost would return there.

sentences.zh: 」勒以百姓始復業，資儲未豐，於是重制禁釀，郊祀宗廟皆以醴酒，行之數年，無復釀者。

translations.literal: ” Le, because the common people were only beginning to return to their occupations and stores were not yet abundant, therefore heavily regulated and forbade brewing; suburban sacrifices and ancestral temple rites all used sweet ale, and for several years practiced this until there were none who brewed again.
translations.idiomatic: ” Grain was still short, so he banned private brewing, supplied suburban and temple rites with sweet rice wine instead, and within a few years liquor had vanished from the market.

sentences.zh: 尋署石季龍為車騎將軍，率騎三萬討鮮卑郁粥于離石，俘獲及牛馬十餘萬，郁粥奔烏丸，悉降其眾城。

translations.literal: Soon he appointed Shi Tigun General of Chariots and Cavalry, leading thirty thousand horse to campaign against the Xianbei Yuzhu at Lishi, capturing men and cattle and horses over one hundred thousand; Yuzhu fled to the Wuhuan, and all his walled settlements submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Shi Hu led thirty thousand cavalry against the Xianbei chief Yuzhu at Lishi, took a hundred thousand captives and animals, drove Yuzhu to the Wuhuan, and forced every town in his orbit to surrender.

sentences.zh: 先是，勒世子興死，至是，立子弘為世子，領中領軍。

translations.literal: Earlier, Le’s heir apparent Xing had died; at this point he established his son Hong as heir apparent, heading the central palace guard.
translations.idiomatic: After the death of heir Shi Xing, Shi Le named Shi Hong crown prince and central guard commander.

sentences.zh: 遣季龍統中外精卒四萬討徐龕，龕堅守不戰，於是築室返耕，列長圍以守之。

translations.literal: He sent Tigun to command forty thousand picked troops of inner and outer armies to punish Xu Kan; Kan held fast and would not fight, whereupon they built huts, turned plows backward, and laid a long cordon to besiege him.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu invested Xu Kan with forty thousand veterans; Kan refused battle, so Hu’s men farmed behind siege lines and waited him out.

sentences.zh: 晉鎮北將軍劉隗降於勒，拜鎮南將軍，封列侯。

translations.literal: Jin’s General Who Guards the North, Liu Wei, surrendered to Le and was appointed General Who Guards the South, enfeoffed a full marquis.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Wei, Jin’s northern guardian, defected and received a southern command and full marquisate.

sentences.zh: 石季龍攻陷徐龕，送之襄國，勒囊盛于百尺樓自上Ξ殺之，令步都等妻子刳而食之，坑龕降卒三千。

translations.literal: Shi Tigun stormed Xu Kan, sent him to Xiangguo; Le sewed him in a sack at a hundred-foot tower and killed him from above; he ordered Budu’s and others’ wives and children to disembowel and eat him, and buried alive three thousand of Kan’s surrendered soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu took Xu Kan alive to Xiangguo, where Shi Le sewed him into a sack, hoisted him to a hundred-foot tower, and had him executed from above; he then forced Wang Budu’s family to carve him up for food and buried three thousand of Kan’s surrendered troops alive.

sentences.zh: 晉兗州刺史劉遐懼，自鄒山退屯於下邳。

translations.literal: Jin’s Inspector of Yanzhou, Liu Xia, feared, and from Zou Mountain withdrew to encamp at Xiapi.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhou governor Liu Xia, unnerved, pulled back from Zou Mountain to Xiapi.

sentences.zh: 琅邪內史孫默以琅邪叛降於勒。

translations.literal: Langye interior secretary Sun Mo took Langye in revolt and surrendered to Le.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Mo, interior secretary of Langye, handed that commandery to Shi Le.

sentences.zh: 徐兗間壘壁多送任請降，皆就拜守宰。

translations.literal: Many stockades between Xu and Yan sent hostages asking to surrender, and all were thereupon appointed guards and magistrates.
translations.idiomatic: Forts along the Xu–Yan border sent hostages and received magistrates in return.

sentences.zh: 清河張披為程遐長史，遐甚委昵之，張賓舉為別駕，引參政事。

translations.literal: Qinghe’s Zhang Pi was chief clerk to Cheng Xia; Xia greatly entrusted and favored him; Zhang Bin recommended him as aide-de-camp and brought him into government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Pi of Qinghe served Cheng Xia as chief clerk, won his confidence, and was promoted by Zhang Bin to aide-de-camp with a voice in policy.

sentences.zh: 遐疾披去己，又惡賓之權盛。

translations.literal: Xia resented that Pi had been taken away from him and also hated Bin’s excessive power.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Xia bitterly resented Zhang Pi’s transfer off his staff and envied Zhang Bin’s ascendancy.

sentences.zh: 勒世子弘，即遐之甥也，自以有援，欲收威重於朝，乃使弘之母譖之曰：「張披與張賓為遊俠，門客日百餘乘，物望皆歸之，非社稷之利也，宜除披以便國家。

translations.literal: Le’s heir Hong was Xia’s nephew; trusting he had backing, he wished to gather awe and weight at court, and so had Hong’s mother slander, saying, “Zhang Pi and Zhang Bin were wandering knights; their retainers exceed a hundred carriages daily; men’s hopes all go to them—it is not to the altars of soil and grain’s benefit; Pi ought to be removed to benefit the state.”
translations.idiomatic: Heir Shi Hong was Cheng Xia’s nephew; through his mother Cheng whispered to Shi Le that Zhang Pi and Zhang Bin still behaved like bravos with a hundred-horse retinue, drawing all prestige to themselves—“cut Pi away for the good of the state.”

sentences.zh: 」勒然之。

translations.literal: ” Le assented.
translations.idiomatic: ” Shi Le agreed.

sentences.zh: 至是，披取急召不時至，因此遂殺之。

translations.literal: At this point Pi took urgent leave and when summoned did not arrive promptly; on this basis he was then killed.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Zhang Pi failed to answer an urgent summons, Shi Le used that excuse to put him to death.

sentences.zh: 賓知遐之間己，遂弗敢請。

translations.literal: Bin knew that Xia had slandered him, and therefore did not dare to make his request.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Cheng Xia’s malice toward him, Zhang Bin held his tongue and pressed no petition.

sentences.zh: 無幾，以遐為右長史，總執朝政，自是朝臣莫不震懼，赴于程氏矣。

translations.literal: Before long, Xia was made right chief clerk, with overall charge of court government; from this the court ministers all trembled with fear and submitted to the Cheng clan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Cheng Xia became chief clerk of the right and ran the administration; the rest of the bureaucracy quailed and fell into line behind the Chengs.

sentences.zh: 時祖逖卒，勒始侵寇邊戍。

translations.literal: At that time Zu Ti died, and only then did Le begin to invade and raid the border garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: Once Zu Ti was dead, Shi Le finally ventured to probe the frontier again.

sentences.zh: 勒征虜石他敗王師於酂西，執將軍衛榮而歸。

translations.literal: Le’s General Who Captures Foes, Shi Ta, defeated the royal army west of Zan, seized General Wei Rong, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Ta, Shi Le’s “captor of enemies” general, routed an imperial column west of Zan, took General Wei Rong prisoner, and marched back.

sentences.zh: 征北將軍祖約懼，退如壽春。

translations.literal: General Who Conquers the North Zu Yue feared and withdrew to Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Yue, who held the northern command, lost his nerve and pulled back to Shouchun.

sentences.zh: 勒境內大疫，死者十二三，乃罷徽文殿作。

translations.literal: A great pestilence raged within Le’s borders; of those who died, two or three in ten, so he stopped work on the Huiwen Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Epidemic disease carried off perhaps a fifth of the population within his realm, forcing him to halt construction of the Huiwen Hall.

sentences.zh: 遣其將王陽屯於豫州，有窺窬之志，於是兵難日尋，梁鄭之間騷然矣。

translations.literal: He sent his general Wang Yang to encamp at Yuzhou with designs of encroachment; from this military disasters followed day after day, and between Liang and Zheng there was turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: He stationed Wang Yang in Yuzhou with an eye toward expansion; fighting flared almost daily, and the country between the Liang and Zheng regions seethed.

sentences.zh: 又遣季龍統中外步騎四萬討曹嶷。

translations.literal: Again he sent Tigun to command forty thousand foot and horse of inner and outer armies to punish Cao Yi.
translations.idiomatic: He again dispatched Shi Hu at the head of forty thousand mixed troops to bring Cao Yi to heel.

sentences.zh: 先是，嶷議欲徙海中，保根餘山，會疾疫甚，計未及就。

translations.literal: Earlier, Yi had planned to move into the sea and hold Gengyu Mountain, but a severe sickness struck and the plan was not completed in time.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Yi had meant to evacuate into the offshore islands and fortify Mount Gengyu, but raging disease overtook him before the scheme could mature.

sentences.zh: 季龍進兵圍廣固，東萊太守劉巴、長廣太守呂披皆以郡降。

translations.literal: Tigun advanced and surrounded Guanggu; Donglai Administrator Liu Ba and Changguang Administrator Lü Pi each surrendered their commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu closed the ring around Guanggu, whereupon Liu Ba of Donglai and Lü Pi of Changguang handed over their jurisdictions.

sentences.zh: 以石他為征東將軍，擊羌胡於河西。

translations.literal: He appointed Shi Ta General Who Campaigns East and struck Qiang and Hu peoples west of the River.
translations.idiomatic: He named Shi Ta eastern-expedition commander and sent him against the Qiang and Hu west of the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 左軍石挺濟師於廣固，曹嶷降，送于襄國。

translations.literal: Left Army Shi Ting crossed troops to Guanggu; Cao Yi surrendered and was sent to Xiangguo.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Ting’s left army forded the relief column into Guanggu; Cao Yi capitulated and was shipped to Xiangguo.

sentences.zh: 勒害之，坑其眾三萬。

translations.literal: Le had him killed and buried alive his host of thirty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le executed him and had thirty thousand of his followers thrown into a pit.

sentences.zh: 季龍將盡殺嶷眾，其青州刺史劉征曰：「今留征，使牧人也；

translations.literal: Tigun was about to slaughter Yi’s entire following when Qingzhou Inspector Liu Zheng said, “If you leave Zheng here, Zheng will herd the people for you;
translations.idiomatic: As Shi Hu prepared to massacre Cao Yi’s army, Qingzhou governor Liu Zheng pleaded: “Station me here and I will govern this populace for you;

sentences.zh: 無人焉牧，征將歸矣。

translations.literal: if there are no people, what is there to herd? Zheng will go home.”
translations.idiomatic: without commoners I would have nothing to rule, and I would simply withdraw.”

sentences.zh: 」季龍乃留男女七百口配征，鎮廣固。

translations.literal: ” Tigun then left seven hundred males and females assigned to Zheng to garrison Guanggu.
translations.idiomatic: ” Shi Hu relented, leaving seven hundred men and women with Liu Zheng to hold Guanggu.

sentences.zh: 青州諸郡縣壘壁盡陷。

translations.literal: Stockaded cities and counties throughout Qingzhou all fell.
translations.idiomatic: Every walled town in Qingzhou fell to him.

sentences.zh: 勒司州刺史石生攻晉揚武將軍郭誦于陽翟，不克，進寇襄城，俘獲千餘而還。

translations.literal: Le’s Inspector of Sizhou, Shi Sheng, attacked Jin’s General Who Displays Might Guo Song at Yangdi but did not take him, advanced to raid Xiangcheng, captured over a thousand, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Sheng, Shi Le’s Sizhou governor, failed against Guo Song at Yangdi, pushed on to plunder Xiangcheng, took more than a thousand captives, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 勒以參軍樊垣清貧，擢授章武內史。

translations.literal: Le, because Adjutant Fan Yuan was poor yet incorrupt, promoted him to interior secretary of Zhangwu.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that adjutant Fan Yuan lived in upright poverty, Shi Le promoted him to interior secretary of Zhangwu.

sentences.zh: 既而入辭，勒見坦衣冠弊壞，大驚曰：「樊參軍何貧之甚也！

translations.literal: When shortly afterward he entered to take leave of him, Le saw that Yuan’s cap and gown were worn out and exclaimed in alarm, “Adjutant Fan, how extreme is your poverty!”
translations.idiomatic: When Fan Yuan came to bid farewell, Shi Le saw his threadbare court dress and cried, “Counselor Fan, you are poorer than anyone I have seen!”

sentences.zh: 」坦性誠樸，率然而對曰：「頃遭羯賊無道，資財蕩盡。

translations.literal: ” Yuan’s nature was honest and plain; he bluntly replied, “Lately I met the lawless Jie bandits and my goods were utterly swept away.”
translations.idiomatic: ” Fan Yuan answered plainly: “The Jie raiders left me nothing—they stripped me clean.”

sentences.zh: 」勒笑曰：「羯賊乃爾暴掠邪！

translations.literal: ” Le laughed and said, “So Jie bandits are that violent in plundering!”
translations.idiomatic: ” Shi Le laughed: “So our Jie boys helped themselves that thoroughly?”

sentences.zh: 今當相償耳。

translations.literal: ” “Now I shall compensate you.”
translations.idiomatic: ” “Then let me make it up to you.”

sentences.zh: 」坦大懼，叩頭泣謝。

translations.literal: ” Yuan was greatly frightened, knocked his head and wept in apology.
translations.idiomatic: ” Fan Yuan went pale, kowtowed, and begged forgiveness in tears.

sentences.zh: 勒曰：「孤律自防俗士，不關卿輩老書生也。

translations.literal: ” Le said, “My statutes are meant to guard against vulgar fellows; they do not concern old scholars like you.”
translations.idiomatic: ” Shi Le said, “Those laws are for coarse upstarts, not for a bookish elder like you.”

sentences.zh: 」賜車馬衣服裝錢三百萬，以勵貪俗。

translations.literal: ” He bestowed carriage, horses, clothes, and three million in cash to encourage the greedy custom.
translations.idiomatic: ” He gave him a carriage, horses, robes, and three million cash to shame the grasping ways at court.

sentences.zh: 勒將兵都尉石瞻寇下邳，敗晉將軍劉長，遂寇蘭陵，又敗彭城內史劉續。

translations.literal: Le’s Colonel of the Army, Shi Zhan, raided Xiapi, defeated Jin General Liu Chang, then raided Lanling, and again defeated Pengcheng Interior Secretary Liu Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Colonel Shi Zhan struck Xiapi, routed Jin’s Liu Chang, pushed into Lanling, and beat Liu Xu, the Pengcheng interior secretary.

sentences.zh: 東莞太守竺珍、東海太守蕭誕以郡叛降於勒。

translations.literal: Dongguan Administrator Zhu Zhen and Donghai Administrator Xiao Dan rebelled with their commanderies and surrendered to Le.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Zhen of Dongguan and Xiao Dan of Donghai threw over Jin and opened their districts to Shi Le.

sentences.zh: 勒親臨大小學，考諸學生經義，尤高者賞帛有差。

translations.literal: Le personally attended the lesser and greater schools, examined the students on canonical texts, and for the highest achievers bestowed graded silks.
translations.idiomatic: He visited the primary and advanced academies in person, examined pupils on the Classics, and handed out silk prizes to the top scorers.

sentences.zh: 勒雅好文學，雖在軍旅，常令儒生讀史書而聽之，每以其意論古帝王善惡，朝賢儒士聽者莫不歸美焉。

translations.literal: Le by nature loved letters; even in the army he regularly ordered Confucian scholars to read histories aloud while he listened, and each time gave his opinion on ancient emperors’ good and evil; court worthies and scholars who listened had none who did not praise him.
translations.idiomatic: He loved belles-lettres: on campaign he still had literati read histories to him, then held forth on which emperors were virtuous or wicked, to the delight of every adviser within earshot.

sentences.zh: 嘗使人讀《漢書》，聞酈食其勸立六國後，大驚曰：「此法當失，何得遂成天下！

translations.literal: Once he had someone read the Han shu; hearing that Li Yiji urged enthroning the descendants of the Six States, he cried in alarm, “That method ought to have failed—how could it have succeeded in winning the realm!”
translations.idiomatic: Once, while listening to the Book of Han, he heard how Li Yiji pushed Liu Bang to restore the Six States’ lines and cried, “That policy should have ruined everything—how did they still conquer the realm?”

sentences.zh: 」至留侯諫，乃曰：「賴有此耳。

translations.literal: ” When it came to the Marquis of Liu’s remonstrance, he said, “It was lucky this existed.”
translations.idiomatic: ” When the reader reached Zhang Liang’s rebuke, he said, “Thank heaven someone stopped it.”

sentences.zh: 」其天資英達如此。

translations.literal: ” His Heaven-given acumen was acute in this way.
translations.idiomatic: ” Such flashes showed how keen his mind was.

sentences.zh: 勒征徐、揚州兵，會石瞻於下邳，劉遐懼，又自下邳奔於泗汭。

translations.literal: Le levied troops from Xu and Yang provinces, joined Shi Zhan at Xiapi; Liu Xia feared and again fled from Xiapi to the Si estuary.
translations.idiomatic: He drafted soldiers from Xu and Yang to rendezvous with Shi Zhan below Xiapi; Liu Xia, unnerved, bolted from Xiapi toward the Si marshes.

sentences.zh: 石生攻劉曜河內太守尹平于新安，斬之，克壘壁十餘，降掠五千餘戶而歸。

translations.literal: Shi Sheng attacked Liu Yao’s Administrator of Henei, Yin Ping, at Xin’an, beheaded him, took more than ten stockades, and returned after reducing and carrying off over five thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Sheng caught Liu Yao’s Henei governor Yin Ping at Xin’an, killed him, stormed a dozen forts, and came back with five thousand surrendered households and spoils.

sentences.zh: 自是劉、石禍結，兵戈日交，河東、弘農間百姓無聊矣。

translations.literal: From this the Liu–Shi calamity was tied in a knot; arms clashed daily, and the common people between Hedong and Hongnong had no respite.
translations.idiomatic: After that Liu Yao and Shi Le were locked in endless war, and the people between Hedong and Hongnong knew no peace.

sentences.zh: 以右常侍霍皓為勸課大夫，與典農使者硃表、典勸都尉陸充等循行州郡，核定戶籍，勸課農桑。

translations.literal: He appointed Right Permanent Attendant Hu Hao as Commissioner for Exhorting Agriculture, who with Agrarian Commissioner Zhu Biao and Commissioner for Encouragement Lu Chong and others toured provinces and commanderies, verified household registers, and urged farming and sericulture.
translations.idiomatic: He named Hu Hao right permanent attendant and commissioner for agriculture, paired him with agrarian agents Zhu Biao and Lu Chong, and sent them province-wide to audit registers and push tillage.

sentences.zh: 農桑最修者賜五大夫。

translations.literal: Those who most cultivated farming and sericulture were granted the rank of Senior Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: The finest farming communities won the honorary rank of “senior grandee.”

sentences.zh: 使石生自延壽關出寇許潁，俘獲萬餘，降者二萬，生遂攻陷康城。

translations.literal: He had Shi Sheng issue from Yanshou Pass to raid Xu and Ying, capturing over ten thousand and receiving the surrender of twenty thousand; Sheng thereupon stormed and took Kangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Sheng burst from Yanshou Pass into Xu and Ying, took ten thousand prisoners and twenty thousand capitulators, then seized Kangcheng.

sentences.zh: 晉將軍郭誦追生，生大敗，死者千餘。

translations.literal: Jin General Guo Song pursued Sheng; Sheng was heavily defeated, and over a thousand died.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Song chased Shi Sheng, broke his army, and left more than a thousand dead on the field.

sentences.zh: 生收散卒，屯于康城。

translations.literal: Sheng gathered scattered troops and encamped at Kangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Sheng rallied his broken units and dug in at Kangcheng.

sentences.zh: 勒汲郡內史石聰聞生敗，馳救之，進攻郭默，俘獲男女二千餘人。

translations.literal: Le’s Interior Secretary of Ji commandery, Shi Cong, hearing of Sheng’s defeat, galloped to rescue him, advanced to attack Guo Mo, and captured over two thousand men and women.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Cong, Ji’s interior secretary under Shi Le, raced to relieve him, fell on Guo Mo, and took two thousand captives.

sentences.zh: 石聰攻敗晉將李矩、郭默等。

translations.literal: Shi Cong attacked and defeated Jin generals Li Ju, Guo Mo, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Cong went on to crush Li Ju, Guo Mo, and their allies.

sentences.zh: 勒將狩於近郊，主簿程琅諫曰：「劉、馬刺客，離布如林，變起倉卒，帝王亦一夫之敵耳。

translations.literal: Le was about to hunt in the near suburbs when chief clerk Cheng Lang remonstrated: “Liu and Ma are assassins; their agents stand thick as a forest—if a coup bursts forth suddenly, even a Son of Heaven is only the match of one man.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Le planned a hunt near the capital, Cheng Lang warned: “Liu and Ma still field killers; a surprise strike could leave even an emperor as helpless as any commoner.

sentences.zh: 孫策之禍可不慮乎！

translations.literal: Can the disaster of Sun Ce go unconsidered!”
translations.idiomatic: Have you forgotten how Sun Ce died?”

sentences.zh: 且枯木朽株盡能為害，馳騁之弊，今古戒之。

translations.literal: Moreover withered trees and rotten stumps can all do harm; the harm of reckless riding is warned against in past and present.”
translations.idiomatic: Even a dead branch can kill a rider; history is full of warnings about reckless hunts.”

sentences.zh: 」勒勃然曰：「吾幹力自可，足能裁量。

translations.literal: ” Le flared up and said, “My strength is adequate on its own and fully able to measure matters.”
translations.idiomatic: ” Shi Le snapped, “I am strong enough to judge such risks myself.”

sentences.zh: 但知卿文書事，不須白此輩也。

translations.literal: ” “I only need you for paperwork affairs; you need not report on this sort.”
translations.idiomatic: ” “Stick to your documents—stay out of my sport.”

sentences.zh: 」是日逐獸，馬觸木而死，勒亦幾殆，乃曰：「不用忠臣言，吾之過也。

translations.literal: ” That day, chasing game, his horse struck a tree and died, and Le himself was nearly killed; then he said, “Not to use loyal ministers’ words is my fault.”
translations.idiomatic: ” That day his mount hit a tree and threw him; shaken, he said, “Ignoring loyal advice was my mistake.”

sentences.zh: 」乃賜琅朝服錦絹，爵關內侯。

translations.literal: ” Thereupon he bestowed on Lang court dress of brocade and silk and the noble rank of marquis within the passes.
translations.idiomatic: ” He rewarded Cheng Lang with court silks and a marquis-within-the-passes title.

sentences.zh: 於是朝臣謁見，忠言競進矣。

translations.literal: From this, when court ministers had audience, loyal words competed to advance.
translations.idiomatic: After that his officials vied to speak frankly at audience.

sentences.zh: 晉都尉魯潛叛，以許昌降於勒。

translations.literal: Jin Commandant Lu Qian rebelled and surrendered Xuchang to Le.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Qian, a Jin commandant, mutinied and handed Xuchang to Shi Le.

sentences.zh: 石瞻攻陷晉兗州刺史檀斌于鄒山，斌死之。

translations.literal: Shi Zhan stormed and took Jin’s Inspector of Yanzhou, Tan Bin, at Zou Mountain; Bin died in it.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Zhan trapped Jin’s Yanzhou governor Tan Bin on Zou Mountain and killed him in the assault.

sentences.zh: 勒西夷中郎將王勝襲殺并州刺史崔琨、上黨內史王昚，以并州叛於勒。

translations.literal: Le’s Western Yi Leader of Court Gentlemen, Wang Sheng, made a surprise attack killing Inspector of Bingzhou Cui Kun and Interior Secretary of Shangdang Wang Shen, and with Bingzhou rebelled against Le.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sheng, Shi Le’s “western barbarian” court-gentleman leader, murdered Bingzhou governor Cui Kun and Shangdang interior secretary Wang Shen and seized Bingzhou in revolt.

sentences.zh: 先是，石季龍攻劉曜將劉岳於石梁，至是，石梁潰，執岳送襄國。

translations.literal: Earlier, Shi Tigun had attacked Liu Yao’s general Liu Yue at Shiliang; at this point Shiliang collapsed, and Yue was seized and sent to Xiangguo.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Shi Hu had besieged Liu Yue at Shiliang for Liu Yao; the bastion now fell, and Liu Yue was sent in chains to Xiangguo.

sentences.zh: 季龍又攻王勝於并州，殺之。

translations.literal: Tigun again attacked Wang Sheng at Bingzhou and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu then marched on Wang Sheng in Bingzhou and executed him.

sentences.zh: 李矩以劉嶽之敗也，懼，自滎陽遁歸。

translations.literal: Li Ju, because of Liu Yue’s defeat, feared and fled from Xingyang back homeward.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ju, terrified by Liu Yue’s rout, abandoned Xingyang and ran.

sentences.zh: 矩長史崔宣率矩眾二千降於勒。

translations.literal: Ju’s chief clerk Cui Xuan led two thousand of Ju’s host to surrender to Le.
translations.idiomatic: His chief clerk Cui Xuan led two thousand of his men over to Shi Le.

sentences.zh: 於是盡有司之地，徐豫濱淮諸郡縣皆降之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he wholly possessed the lands of Si, and the commanderies and counties along the Huai in Xu and Yu all surrendered to him.
translations.idiomatic: He now held the whole Sizhou pocket, and every county along the Huai in Xu and Yu submitted.

sentences.zh: 勒命徙洛陽晷影于襄國，列之單于庭。

translations.literal: Le ordered the Luoyang sundial’s shadow-rod moved to Xiangguo and arrayed it in the Chanyu court.
translations.idiomatic: He transferred Luoyang’s gnomon and shadow scale to Xiangguo and set them up in the Chanyu yard.

sentences.zh: 銘佐命功臣三十九人于石函，置於建德前殿。

translations.literal: He had the thirty-nine ministers who aided the founding inscribed on stone and placed in a casket before the Jiande front hall.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty-nine founding ministers were named on stone tablets kept in a coffer before Jiande Hall.

sentences.zh: 立桑梓苑于襄國。

translations.literal: He established the Mulberry-and-Homestead Park at Xiangguo.
translations.idiomatic: He laid out a “native-place” park of mulberries at Xiangguo.

sentences.zh: 勒嘗夜微行，檢察營衛，齎繒帛金銀以賂門者求出。

translations.literal: Le once by night went in disguise to inspect camp guards, carrying silks, bolts, gold, and silver to bribe gatekeepers for exit.
translations.idiomatic: He once roamed the palisades at night in plain clothes, offering gold and silk to sentries to see whether they would let him pass.

sentences.zh: 永昌門門候王假欲收捕之，從者至，乃止。

translations.literal: The Yongchang Gate gate warden Wang Jia wished to seize him; when followers arrived, he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The Yongchang gate warden Wang Jia moved to arrest him until escorts arrived and revealed who he was.

sentences.zh: 旦召假以為振忠都尉，爵關內侯。

translations.literal: At dawn he summoned Jia and appointed him Colonel Who Shakes Loyalty, with noble rank marquis within the passes.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn he promoted Wang Jia to “colonel who rouses loyalty” and enfeoffed him marquis within the passes.

sentences.zh: 勒如苑鄉，召記室參軍徐光，光醉不至。

translations.literal: Le went to Yuanxiang and summoned secretary-adjutant Xu Guang, but Guang, drunk, did not come.
translations.idiomatic: Visiting Yuanxiang, he called for Xu Guang; the secretary stayed drunk and ignored the summons.

sentences.zh: 以光物情所湊，常不平之，因此發怒，退為牙門。

translations.literal: Because Guang was where popular sentiment gathered, Le often nursed resentment against him; on this account he flared with anger and reduced him to camp gate.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Guang’s popularity had long irked him; this snub enraged him, and he busted Xu down to gate guard.

sentences.zh: 勒自苑鄉如鄴，徐光侍直，慍然攘袂振紛，仰視不顧。

translations.literal: Le went from Yuanxiang to Ye; Xu Guang was on attendant duty, sullenly rolling up his sleeves, shaking dust from his clothes, looking upward and paying no heed.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Le rode on to Ye, Xu Guang—still on duty—sulkily rolled his sleeves, brushed off his gown, and stared past his sovereign.

sentences.zh: 勒因而惡之，讓光曰：「何負卿而敢怏怏邪！

translations.literal: Le therefore hated him and rebuked Guang, saying, “In what have I wronged you that you dare be so disgruntled!”
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le, furious, snapped, “What grievance makes you wear that scowl?”

sentences.zh: 」於是幽光並其妻子于獄。

translations.literal: ” Thereupon he imprisoned Guang together with his wife and children.
translations.idiomatic: ” He threw Xu Guang and his family into prison.

sentences.zh: 勒既將營鄴宮，又欲以其世子弘為鎮，密與程遐謀之。

translations.literal: Le, since he was about to build the Ye palaces and also wished to post his heir Hong as garrison commander there, secretly plotted with Cheng Xia.
translations.idiomatic: Planning new palaces at Ye and wanting crown prince Shi Hong to hold the city, he took Cheng Xia into his confidence.

sentences.zh: 石季龍自以勳效之重，仗鄴為基，雅無去意。

translations.literal: Shi Tigun, because of the weight of his merit and achievements, relied on Ye as his base and by nature had no mind to leave.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu, confident in his battlefield record, treated Ye as his personal seat and had no wish to move.

sentences.zh: 及修構三台，遷其家室，季龍深恨遐，遣左右數十人夜入遐宅，奸其妻女，掠衣物而去。

translations.literal: When the Three Terraces were repaired and constructed and his household was moved, Tigun deeply hated Xia; he sent several tens of henchmen by night into Xia’s residence, violated his wife and daughters, and carried off clothing goods.
translations.idiomatic: When the Three Terraces project forced Shi Hu’s household to relocate, he blamed Cheng Xia and sent dozens of thugs to rape Cheng’s women and loot his house by night.

sentences.zh: 勒以弘鎮鄴，配禁兵萬人，車騎所統五十四營悉配之，以驍騎領門臣祭酒王陽專統六夷以輔之。

translations.literal: Le posted Hong to garrison Ye, assigning him ten thousand palace guards; the fifty-four camps commanded by chariots and cavalry were all assigned to him, and fierce-cavalry Leader of Libationers for Gate Disciples Wang Yang was solely set to command the Six Yi to assist him.
translations.idiomatic: He installed Shi Hong at Ye with ten thousand household troops and attached all fifty-four camps of the chariotry command; Wang Yang was put over the “six barbarian” corps as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 石聰攻壽春，不克，遂寇逡遒、阜陵，殺掠五千餘人，京師大震。

translations.literal: Shi Cong attacked Shouchun but did not take it, then raided Junqiu and Fuling, killing and plundering over five thousand persons, so the capital region was greatly shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Cong failed at Shouchun but savaged Junqiu and Fuling, killing or seizing five thousand souls and rattling the capital.

sentences.zh: 濟岷太守劉闓、將軍張闔等叛，害下邳內史夏侯嘉，以下邳降于石生。

translations.literal: Jimin Administrator Liu Kai, General Zhang Ge, and others rebelled, killed Xiapi Interior Secretary Xiahou Jia, and with Xiapi surrendered to Shi Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kai of Jimin and Zhang Ge mutinied, murdered Xiapi’s Xiahou Jia, and delivered the city to Shi Sheng.

sentences.zh: 石瞻攻河南太守王羨于邾，陷之。

translations.literal: Shi Zhan attacked Jin’s Administrator of Henan, Wang Xian, at Zhu and took him.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Zhan stormed Henan governor Wang Xian at Zhu and broke the defense.

sentences.zh: 龍驤將軍王國叛，以南郡降於勒。

translations.literal: General Who Prances the Dragon Wang Guo rebelled and with Nan commandery surrendered to Le.
translations.idiomatic: Dragon-prancing general Wang Guo revolted and handed Nan commandery to Shi Le.

sentences.zh: 晉彭城內史劉續復據蘭陵、石城，石瞻攻陷之。

translations.literal: Jin’s Pengcheng Interior Secretary Liu Xu again held Lanling and Shicheng; Shi Zhan stormed and took them.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xu, Pengcheng’s interior secretary, reoccupied Lanling and Shicheng until Shi Zhan retook both.

sentences.zh: 勒令州郡，有墳發掘不掩覆者推劾之，骸骨暴露者縣為備棺衾之具。

translations.literal: Le ordered provinces and commanderies: where tombs had been opened and not re-covered, investigate them; where bones lay exposed, let the county prepare coffins and shrouds.
translations.idiomatic: He told every province to rebury looted graves and supply coffins wherever bones still lay bare.

sentences.zh: 以牙門將王波為記室參軍，典定九流，始立秀、孝試經之制。

translations.literal: He appointed camp-gate general Wang Bo secretary-adjutant, to codify the nine currents; he first established the system of examining classics for the cultivated and filial.
translations.idiomatic: He made gate general Wang Bo secretary, sorted the nine ranks of talent, and introduced classical exams for xiucai and xiaoliao candidates.

sentences.zh: 茌平令師歡獲黑兔，獻之于勒，程遐等以為勒「龍飛革命之祥，于晉以水承金，兔陰精之獸，玄為水色，此示殿下宜速副天人之望也。

translations.literal: Chiping Magistrate Shi Huan captured a black rabbit and presented it to Le; Cheng Lang and others held that for Le it was “an omen of dragon-flight and dynastic change: toward Jin, water succeeds metal; the rabbit is a creature of yin essence, black is water’s color—this shows Your Highness should quickly answer Heaven and men’s hopes.”
translations.idiomatic: Chiping magistrate Shi Huan offered a black hare; Cheng Xia’s clique called it a portent of new mandate—water succeeding Jin’s metal, black matching water—and urged Shi Le to claim heaven’s mandate at once.

sentences.zh: 」於是大赦，以咸和三年改年曰太和。

translations.literal: ” Thereupon a great amnesty was declared, and in the third year of Xianhe the era name was changed to Taihe.
translations.idiomatic: ” He proclaimed a general amnesty and, though Jin still called the year Xianhe 3, his court retitled the era Great Harmony.

sentences.zh: 石堪攻晉豫州刺史祖約于壽春，屯師淮上。

translations.literal: Shi Kan attacked Jin’s Inspector of Yuzhou, Zu Yue, at Shouchun, encamping the army on the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Kan besieged Zu Yue in Shouchun and camped the army along the Huai.

sentences.zh: 晉龍驤將軍王國以南郡叛降於堪。

translations.literal: Jin’s General Who Prances the Dragon Wang Guo rebelled with Nan commandery and surrendered to Kan.
translations.idiomatic: Jin’s dragon-prancing general Wang Guo repeated his mutiny, yielding Nan commandery to Shi Kan.

sentences.zh: 南陽都尉董幼叛，率襄陽之眾又降於堪。

translations.literal: Nanyang Commandant Dong You rebelled and led the host of Xiangyang again to surrender to Kan.
translations.idiomatic: Nanyang commandant Dong You rose with the Xiangyang garrison and went over to Shi Kan as well.

sentences.zh: 祖約諸將佐皆陰遣使附於勒。

translations.literal: Zu Yue’s generals and adjutants all secretly sent envoys to attach themselves to Le.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Yue’s officers were secretly suing for Shi Le’s protection.

sentences.zh: 石聰與堪濟淮，陷壽春，祖約奔曆陽，壽春百姓陷於聰者二萬餘戶。

translations.literal: Shi Cong and Kan crossed the Huai, took Shouchun; Zu Yue fled to Liyang; over twenty thousand households of Shouchun commoners fell into Cong’s hands.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Cong joined Shi Kan across the Huai, seized Shouchun, drove Zu Yue toward Liyang, and enslaved more than twenty thousand city households.

sentences.zh: 劉曜敗季龍于高候，遂圍洛陽。

translations.literal: Liu Yao defeated Tigun at Gaohou, then besieged Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao routed Shi Hu at Gaohou and threw a cordon around Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 勒滎陽太守尹矩、野王太守張進等皆降之，襄國大震。

translations.literal: Le’s Administrator of Xingyang, Yin Ju, Administrator of Yewang, Zhang Jin, and others all surrendered to him; Xiangguo was greatly shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le’s Xingyang governor Yin Ju and Yewang governor Zhang Jin capitulated to Liu Yao, sending shock waves through Xiangguo.

sentences.zh: 勒將親救洛陽，左右長史、司馬郭敖、程遐等固諫曰：「劉曜乘勝雄盛，難與爭鋒，金墉糧豐，攻之未可卒拔。

translations.literal: Le was about to go in person to rescue Luoyang when left and right chief clerks and marshals Guo Ao, Cheng Xia, and others firmly remonstrated: “Liu Yao rides victory and is fiercely strong—hard to contend with edge to edge; Jinyong is rich in grain and cannot be suddenly taken by assault.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Le prepared a personal relief march on Luoyang, Guo Ao and Cheng Xia argued hard: “Liu Yao is riding high; Jinyong’s granaries make Luoyang a tough nut—you cannot rush him.

sentences.zh: 曜懸軍千里，勢不支久。

translations.literal: Yao’s army hangs a thousand li; its situation cannot support long endurance.
translations.idiomatic: His army is a thousand li from home and cannot keep this up forever.

sentences.zh: 不可親動，動無萬全，大業去矣。

translations.literal: You must not move personally; if you move without perfect safety, the great enterprise is gone.”
translations.idiomatic: Stay off the field—one misstep costs the whole realm.”

sentences.zh: 」勒大怒，按劍叱遐等出。

translations.literal: ” Le was greatly angered, pressed his sword and shouted for Xia and others to leave.
translations.idiomatic: ” Shi Le, livid, hand on sword, roared until the advisers fled.

sentences.zh: 於是赦徐光，召而謂之曰：「劉曜乘高候之勢，圍守洛陽，庸人之情皆謂其鋒不可當也。

translations.literal: Thereupon he amnestied Xu Guang, summoned him, and said to him, “Liu Yao, riding the Gaohou momentum, surrounds and holds Luoyang; in the feeling of common men, all say his edge cannot be withstood.
translations.idiomatic: He then freed Xu Guang and asked, “Liu Yao has Luoyang ringed after Gaohou; cowards say his spear is unstoppable.

sentences.zh: 然曜帶甲十萬，攻一城而百日不克，師老卒殆，以我初銳擊之，可一戰而擒。

translations.literal: Yet Yao brings armored men numbering one hundred thousand, attacks one city yet a hundred days does not take it; the army is weary and the soldiers exhausted—if with our fresh keenness we strike them, in one battle we can capture him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet a hundred thousand men have stalled a hundred days before one wall; his troops are spent. One sharp blow from us finishes him.

sentences.zh: 若洛陽不守，曜必送死冀州，自河已北，席捲南向，吾事去矣。

translations.literal: If Luoyang is not held, Yao is sure to throw his life against Ji Province; from the River northward he will roll up southward, and our affair is gone.”
translations.idiomatic: If Luoyang falls, he will hurl everything at Ji north of the river and sweep south—then we are lost.”

sentences.zh: 程遐等不欲吾親行，卿以為何如？

translations.literal: Cheng Xia and the others do not wish me to go in person—what do you think?”
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Xia does not want me to lead—what say you?”

sentences.zh: 」光對曰：「劉曜乘高候之勢而不能進臨襄國，更守金墉，此其無能為也。

translations.literal: ” Guang replied, “Liu Yao, riding the Gaohou momentum, yet could not advance to face Xiangguo and instead guards Jinyong—this shows his inability.
translations.idiomatic: ” Xu Guang answered: “He won at Gaohou yet dares not march on Xiangguo; he hugs Jinyong instead—that is weakness.

sentences.zh: 懸軍三時，亡攻戰之利，若鸞旗親駕，必望旌奔敗。

translations.literal: His suspended army three seasons lacks the advantage of attack; if the phoenix-banner chariot goes in person, they are sure to flee at sight of the standards.”
translations.idiomatic: Three seasons in the field without a breakthrough—show the imperial banners in person and his host will scatter.”

sentences.zh: 定天下之計，在今一舉。

translations.literal: The plan to settle the realm hangs on this one stroke.
translations.idiomatic: The fate of the empire turns on this single throw.

sentences.zh: 今此機會，所謂天授，授而弗應，禍之攸集。

translations.literal: Now this opportunity is what is called Heaven’s gift; if Heaven gives and you do not answer, calamity will gather.
translations.idiomatic: This is the opening Heaven sends; spurn it and disaster follows.

sentences.zh: 」勒笑曰：「光之言是也。

translations.literal: ” Le laughed and said, “Guang’s words are right.”
translations.idiomatic: ” Shi Le laughed and said, “Xu Guang has the right of it.”

sentences.zh: 」佛圖澄亦謂勒曰：「大軍若出，必擒劉曜。

translations.literal: ” Fotucheng also told Le, “If the great army goes forth, it is sure to capture Liu Yao.”
translations.idiomatic: ” The monk Fotucheng added: “March, and Liu Yao is yours.”

sentences.zh: 」勒尤悅，使內外戒嚴，有諫者斬。

translations.literal: ” Le was especially pleased, ordered inner and outer strict martial law, and said that whoever remonstrated would be beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: ” Shi Le, delighted, declared full mobilization and threatened death to any adviser who objected.

sentences.zh: 命石堪、石聰及豫州刺史桃豹等各統見眾會滎陽，使石季龍進據石門，以左衛石邃都督中軍事，勒統步騎四萬赴金墉，濟自大堨。

translations.literal: He ordered Shi Kan, Shi Cong, and Yuzhou Inspector Tao Bao each to lead their present hosts to assemble at Xingyang, had Shi Tigun advance to hold Shimen, had Left Guard Shi Sui supervise central-army affairs, and himself commanded forty thousand foot and horse to go to Jinyong, crossing from the great weir.
translations.idiomatic: He massed Shi Kan, Shi Cong, and Tao Bao’s Yuzhou troops at Xingyang, sent Shi Hu to seize Shimen, put Shi Sui in charge of the center, and led forty thousand mixed troops toward Jinyong, crossing at the great dike.

sentences.zh: 先是，流澌風猛，軍至，冰泮清和，濟畢，流澌大至，勒以為神靈之助也，命曰靈昌津。

translations.literal: Earlier, drifting ice and fierce wind—when the army arrived, the ice broke up, clear and mild; when the crossing was finished, drifting ice came in great mass; Le held it the aid of spirits and gods and named it Spirit-Prosperity Ford.
translations.idiomatic: Ice had choked the river until his host arrived; then the floes parted and the ford cleared, only to slam shut again once he crossed—omens he christened the Spirit-Prosperity crossing.

sentences.zh: 勒顧謂徐光曰：「曜盛兵成皋關，上計也；

translations.literal: Le turned and said to Xu Guang, “If Yao masses troops at Chenggao Pass, that is the best plan;
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le told Xu Guang: “If Liu Yao blocks Chenggao Pass, he plays the best card;

sentences.zh: 阻洛水，其次也；

translations.literal: to block the Luo River is next best;
translations.idiomatic: holding the Luo line is second best;

sentences.zh: 坐守洛陽者成擒也。

translations.literal: to sit and guard Luoyang is to become a captive.”
translations.idiomatic: sitting tight inside Luoyang hands him to us.”

sentences.zh: 」諸軍集于成皋，步卒六萬，騎二萬七千。

translations.literal: ” The various armies gathered at Chengguo: sixty thousand foot soldiers and twenty-seven thousand horse.
translations.idiomatic: ” Sixty thousand infantry and twenty-seven thousand cavalry closed on Chengguo.

sentences.zh: 勒見曜無守軍，大悅，舉手指天，又自指額曰：「天也！

translations.literal: Le saw that Yao had no defending troops and was greatly pleased; he raised his hand to Heaven, then pointed at his own brow and said, “It is Heaven!”
translations.idiomatic: Seeing no Liu Yao outposts, Shi Le pointed skyward, tapped his brow, and cried, “Heaven fights for me!”

sentences.zh: 」乃卷甲銜枚而詭道兼路，出於鞏、訾之間。

translations.literal: ” Then he rolled armor, had the men hold bits silent, and by secret paths doubled marches, issuing between Gong and Zi.
translations.idiomatic: ” He muffled his men, doubled through byways, and burst from the hills between Gong and Zi.

sentences.zh: 知曜陳其軍十餘萬於城西，彌悅，謂左右曰：「可以賀我矣！

translations.literal: Learning that Yao had drawn up his army of over a hundred thousand west of the city, he was all the more pleased and said to those at his side, “You may congratulate me!”
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Liu Yao had stacked a hundred thousand men west of the walls, he grinned: “Send my congratulations!”

sentences.zh: 」勒統步騎四萬人自宣陽門，升故太極前殿。

translations.literal: ” Le commanded forty thousand foot and horse through Xuanyang Gate and ascended the old Taiji front hall.
translations.idiomatic: ” He led forty thousand troops through Xuanyang Gate onto the old Taiji terrace.

sentences.zh: 季龍步卒三萬，自城北而西，攻其中軍，石堪、石聰等各以精騎八千，城西而北，擊其前鋒，大戰于西陽門。

translations.literal: Tigun’s foot soldiers, thirty thousand, from the city’s north toward the west attacked his center army; Shi Kan, Shi Cong, and others each with eight thousand picked horse from the city’s west toward the north struck his vanguard; a great battle was fought at Xiyang Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu drove thirty thousand foot from the north wall against the enemy center while Shi Kan and Shi Cong swept eight thousand elite horse from the west against Liu Yao’s van at Xiyang Gate.

sentences.zh: 勒躬貫甲胄，出自閶闔，夾擊之。

translations.literal: Le personally donned armor and helm, came out from Changhe Gate, and struck them from both sides.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le buckled on mail, rode out Changhe Gate, and closed the pincers himself.

sentences.zh: 曜軍大潰，石堪執曜，送之以徇於軍，斬首五萬餘級，枕屍于金穀。

translations.literal: Yao’s army was greatly routed; Shi Kan seized Yao, sent him to be displayed through the army, and beheaded over fifty thousand; corpses pillowed the ground from Metal Valley.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao’s line collapsed; Shi Kan took him captive, paraded him through the ranks, and counted fifty thousand heads stacked toward the Metal Valley road.

sentences.zh: 勒下令曰：「所欲擒者一人耳，今已獲之，其敕將士抑鋒止銳，縱其歸命之路。

translations.literal: Le issued an order: “The one I wished to capture is a single man; now he is already taken—let the generals and soldiers blunt edges and halt keenness, opening a road for those who surrender their lives.”
translations.idiomatic: He proclaimed: “I wanted only one man; now that Liu Yao is mine, check the slaughter and let the rest flee.”

sentences.zh: 」乃旋師。

translations.literal: ” Thereupon he turned the army back.
translations.idiomatic: ” Then he marched home.

sentences.zh: 使征東石邃等帥騎衛曜而北。

translations.literal: He had Eastern Campaign Shi Sui and others lead horse to escort Yao northward.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Shi Sui and other eastern commanders to herd Liu Yao north under cavalry guard.

sentences.zh: 及是，祖約舉兵敗，降於勒，勒使王波讓之曰：「卿逆極勢窮，方來歸命，吾朝豈逋逃之藪邪？

translations.literal: When it came to this, Zu Yue raised troops, was defeated, and surrendered to Le; Le had Wang Bo reproach him, saying, “You, at the extreme of rebellion and exhaustion of strength, only now come to surrender your lives—does my court serve as a den for fugitives?
translations.idiomatic: Zu Yue, beaten after his revolt, sued for mercy; Shi Le sent Wang Bo to sneer: “You crawl in only when broken—is my court a hideout for fugitives?

sentences.zh: 而卿敢有靦面目也。

translations.literal: Yet you dare have brazen face.”
translations.idiomatic: And you still show your face?”

sentences.zh: 」示之以前後檄書，乃赦之。

translations.literal: ” He showed him the successive proclamations before and after, then amnestied him.
translations.idiomatic: ” He flung Zu’s own edicts in his face, then spared him.

sentences.zh: 劉曜子熙等去長安，奔於上邽，遣季龍討之。

translations.literal: Liu Yao’s sons Xi and others left Chang’an, fled to Shanggui, and Le sent Tigun to punish them.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao’s heir Liu Xi fled Chang’an for Shanggui; Shi Le sent Shi Hu after him.

sentences.zh: 勒巡行州諸郡，引見高年、孝悌、力田、文學之士，班賜穀帛有差。

translations.literal: Le toured the province’s commanderies, summoned and met the aged, filial, diligent farmers, and men of letters, distributing grain and silk in graded amounts.
translations.idiomatic: He toured the province, interviewed elders, filial sons, diligent farmers, and scholars, and handed out grain and silk by rank.

sentences.zh: 令遠近牧守宣告屬城，諸所欲言，靡有隱諱，使知區區之朝虛渴讜言也。

translations.literal: He ordered near and distant shepherds and guards to proclaim to dependent cities: whatever they wished to say, let none hide it, so they would know how this humble court thirsts for forthright words.
translations.idiomatic: He told every governor to invite unvarnished memorials so the realm would see how hungry his court was for blunt counsel.

sentences.zh: 季龍克上邽，遣主簿趙封送傳國玉璽、金璽、太子玉璽各一於勒。

translations.literal: Tigun took Shanggui and sent chief clerk Zhao Feng to deliver to Le one each of the transmitted-state jade seal, gold seal, and heir-apparent jade seal.
translations.idiomatic: After Shi Hu took Shanggui, chief clerk Zhao Feng brought the imperial jade seal, a gold seal, and the crown prince’s seal to Xiangguo.

sentences.zh: 季龍進攻集木且羌於河西，克之，俘獲數萬，秦、隴悉平。

translations.literal: Tigun advanced to attack the Jumuqie Qiang west of the River, took them, captured several tens of thousands, and Qin and Long were wholly pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu next crushed the Jumuqie Qiang beyond the Yellow River, took tens of thousands captive, and quieted Qin and Long.

sentences.zh: 涼州牧張駿大懼，遣使稱籓，貢方物於勒，徙氐羌十五萬落于司、冀州。

translations.literal: Liangzhou Shepherd Zhang Jun was greatly frightened, sent envoys declaring vassalage, presented local products to Le, and relocated one hundred fifty thousand Di and Qiang households to Si and Ji provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun of Liangzhou, terrified, acknowledged Shi Le’s overlordship, sent tribute, and resettled a hundred fifty thousand Di and Qiang families into Si and Ji.

sentences.zh: 勒群臣議以勒功業既隆，祥符並萃，宜時革徽號以答乾坤之望，於是石季龍等奉皇帝璽綬，上尊號於勒，勒弗許。

translations.literal: Le’s host of ministers deliberated that, because Le’s merit and enterprise were already lofty and auspicious tokens gathered together, the time had come to change his title to answer Heaven and Earth’s hopes; thereupon Shi Tigun and others offered the emperor’s jade and ribbon, presenting the exalted title to Le, but Le did not grant it.
translations.idiomatic: His ministers argued that omens demanded a new style; Shi Hu offered the Han imperial seals, but Shi Le refused the throne.

sentences.zh: 群臣固請，勒乃以咸和五年僭號趙天王，行皇帝事。

translations.literal: The host of ministers firmly requested, and Le then in the fifth year of Xianhe usurped the title King of Heaven of Zhao, exercising Son of Heaven affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Pressed again, in Jin’s fifth Xianhe year he took the unsanctioned title “Heavenly King of Zhao” while acting as emperor.

sentences.zh: 尊其祖邪曰宣王，父周曰元王。

translations.literal: He honored his grandfather Xie as King of Instruction, his father Zhou as Primal King.
translations.idiomatic: He canonized his grandfather Shi Xie as King of Instruction and his father Zhou as Primal King.

sentences.zh: 立其妻劉氏為王后，世子弘為太子。

translations.literal: He established his wife Lady Liu as queen, heir Hong as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: He named Lady Liu queen and Shi Hong crown prince.

sentences.zh: 署其子宏持節、散騎常侍、都督中外諸軍事、驃騎大將軍、大單于，封秦王；

translations.literal: He appointed his son Hong bearer of credentials, cavalier attendant-in-ordinary, supervisor of all military affairs of inner and outer, General of Agile Cavalry, Grand Chanyu, enfeoffing him Prince of Qin;
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hong received credentials, cavalier rank, supreme command, title of agile cavalry general and grand Chanyu, and the princedom of Qin;

sentences.zh: 左衛將軍斌太原王；

translations.literal: Left Guard General Bin as Prince of Taiyuan;
translations.idiomatic: Shi Bin became Prince of Taiyuan while holding the left guard;

sentences.zh: 小子恢為輔國將軍、南陽王；

translations.literal: younger son Hui as General Who Supports the State, Prince of Nanyang;
translations.idiomatic: the younger son Shi Hui became supporting-state general and prince of Nanyang;

sentences.zh: 中山公季龍為太尉、守尚書令、中山王；

translations.literal: Duke of Zhongshan Tigun as grand commandant, acting overseer of the masters of writing, Prince of Zhongshan;
translations.idiomatic: Zhongshan duke Shi Hu became grand commandant, acting chief of the secretariat, and prince of Zhongshan;

sentences.zh: 石生河東王；

translations.literal: Shi Sheng as Prince of Hedong;
translations.idiomatic: Shi Sheng was named prince of Hedong;

sentences.zh: 石堪彭城王；

translations.literal: Shi Kan as Prince of Pengcheng;
translations.idiomatic: Shi Kan became prince of Pengcheng;

sentences.zh: 以季龍子邃為冀州刺史，封齊王，加散騎常侍、武衛將軍；

translations.literal: he appointed Tigun’s son Sui Inspector of Ji, enfeoffed Prince of Qi, adding cavalier attendant-in-ordinary and general who guards martially;
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu’s son Shi Sui took Ji province, the princedom of Qi, cavalier rank, and the martial guard generalship;

sentences.zh: 宣左將軍；

translations.literal: Xuan as General of the Left of the Van;
translations.idiomatic: Shi Xuan became general of the left van;

sentences.zh: 挺侍中、梁王。
