translations.literal: Ting as palace attendant, Prince of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Ting became palace attendant and prince of Liang.

sentences.zh: 署左長史郭敖為尚書左僕射，右長史程遐為右僕射、領吏部尚書，左司馬夔安、右司馬郭殷、從事中郎李鳳、前郎中令裴憲為尚書，署參軍事徐光為中書令、領秘書監。

translations.literal: He appointed left chief clerk Guo Ao as left supervisor of the masters of writing, right chief clerk Cheng Xia as right supervisor and concurrent overseer of the ministry of personnel, left marshal Kui An and right marshal Guo Yin and adjutant Li Feng and former steward of the masters Pei Xian as masters of writing, and secretary-adjutant Xu Guang as palace secretary and concurrent overseer of the secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He named Guo Ao left secretariat director, Cheng Xia right director with personnel portfolio, Kui An and Guo Yin marshals, Li Feng and Pei Xian masters of writing, and Xu Guang palace secretary with charge of the imperial library.

sentences.zh: 論功封爵，開國郡公文武二十一人，侯二十四人，縣公二十六人，侯二十二人，其餘文武各有差。

translations.literal: By merit he enfeoffed nobility: twenty-one civil and military founders as commandery dukes with their own states, twenty-four marquises, twenty-six county dukes, twenty-two marquises; the rest of civil and military each had graded awards.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-one founding ministers became ducal fiefs, plus twenty-four marquises, twenty-six county dukes, and twenty-two lesser marquises; everyone else took graded titles.

sentences.zh: 侍中任播等參議，以趙承金為水德，旗幟尚玄，牲牡尚白，子社醜臘，勒從之。

translations.literal: Attendants Ren Bo and others jointly deliberated that Zhao inheriting Jin’s metal should take water as its virtue, banners esteem black, sacrificial victims esteem white, and set the community sacrifice in the zi month and the year-end offering in the chou month; Le followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Bo’s faction argued that Zhao, succeeding Jin’s metal phase, should adopt water: black standards, white victims, and calendar tweaks for community and year-end rites—Shi Le agreed.

sentences.zh: 勒下書曰：「自今有疑難大事，八坐及委丞郎齎詣東堂，詮詳平決。

translations.literal: Le issued documents saying, “From now on, whenever there are doubtful or great matters, the eight seats and deputy masters-of-writing gentlemen shall carry them to the eastern hall for full discussion and equitable decision.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered: “Whenever policy stumps you, the eight high ministers and secretariat deputies must take the case to the eastern hall for joint adjudication.

sentences.zh: 其有軍國要務須啟，有令僕尚書隨局入陳，勿避寒暑昏夜也。」

translations.literal: Where there are military or state vital matters that must be reported, have the masters of writing enter statements bureau by bureau, not avoiding cold, heat, dusk, or night.”
translations.idiomatic: Military or state emergencies go straight to the secretariat at any hour, winter or summer.”

sentences.zh: 勒以祖約不忠於本朝，誅之，及其諸子至親屬百餘人。

translations.literal: Le, because Zu Yue was not loyal to his own court, executed him together with his sons and close kin over one hundred persons.
translations.idiomatic: Deeming Zu Yue a traitor to Jin, Shi Le executed him with more than a hundred sons and kinsmen.

sentences.zh: 群臣固請勒宜即尊號，勒乃僭即皇帝位，大赦境內，改元曰建平，自襄國都臨漳。

translations.literal: The host of ministers firmly requested that Le ought immediately to assume the exalted title; Le then usurped the emperor’s seat, granted a great amnesty within his borders, changed the era name to Jianping, and moved the capital from Xiangguo to Linzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Forced again, he took the imperial seat, amnestied the realm, declared the Jianping era, and shifted the capital from Xiangguo to Linzhang.

sentences.zh: 追尊其高祖曰順皇，曾祖曰威皇，祖曰宣皇，父曰世宗元皇帝，妣曰元昭皇太后，文武封進各有差。

translations.literal: He posthumously honored his high ancestor as Shun Emperor, great-great-grandfather as Wei Emperor, grandfather as Xuan Emperor, father as Yuan Emperor of the World Temple, mother as Empress Dowager Yuan Zhao; civil and military enfeoffments and promotions each had graded differences.
translations.idiomatic: He stacked posthumous imperial titles on four generations and his mother, and promoted the peerage of his entire court.

sentences.zh: 立其妻劉氏為皇后，又定昭儀、夫人位視上公，貴嬪、貴人視列侯，員各一人；

translations.literal: He established his wife Lady Liu as empress, and further fixed noble consort and madame ranks to equal senior dukes, honored concubine and honored lady to equal full marquises, one person each;
translations.idiomatic: Lady Liu became empress; top consorts were ranked with senior dukes, next ranks with full marquises, one holder each;

sentences.zh: 三英、九華視伯，淑媛、淑儀視子，容華、美人視男，務簡賢淑，不限員數。

translations.literal: Three Blossom and Nine Splendor to equal earls; pure maiden and pure model to equal viscounts; lovely bloom and beauty to equal barons—seeking simplicity and worthiness in the virtuous, with no fixed quota.
translations.idiomatic: lesser harem grades matched earls, viscounts, and barons, filled for talent rather than by quota.

sentences.zh: 勒荊州監軍郭敬、南蠻校尉董幼寇襄陽。

translations.literal: Le’s Jingzhou army supervisor Guo Jing and Colonel of the Southern Man Dong You raided Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Jing, supervising Jingzhou troops for Shi Le, and southern-man colonel Dong You struck Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 勒驛敕敬退屯樊城，戒之使偃藏旗幟，寂若無人，彼若使人觀察，則告之曰：「自愛堅守，後七八日大騎將至，相策不復得走矣。

translations.literal: Le by post-station order commanded Jing to withdraw and encamp at Fancheng, warning him to lay flat and hide banners and standards, silent as if no men were there; if they sent men to observe, then tell them, “We ourselves will stoutly hold the defense; in seven or eight days great horse will arrive—mutually we will plan so that you can no longer flee.”
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le told Guo Jing to fall back to Fancheng, strike the colors, and if probed reply: “We mean to hold out; in a week a great cavalry host arrives—you will not get away.”

sentences.zh: 」敬使人浴馬於津，周而復始，晝夜不絕。

translations.literal: ” Jing had men bathe horses at the ford, circling without cease, day and night unbroken.
translations.idiomatic: ” Guo Jing’s men watered horses at the ford in endless circles day and night.

sentences.zh: 偵諜還告南中郎將周撫，撫以為勒軍大至，懼而奔武昌。

translations.literal: Scouts returned and reported to South Leader of Court Gentlemen Zhou Fu; Fu thought Le’s army had arrived in force, feared, and fled to Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: Spies convinced Zhou Fu that a massive host was coming; he bolted to Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 敬入襄陽，軍無私掠，百姓安之。

translations.literal: Jing entered Xiangyang; the army made no private plunder, and the hundred surnames were settled.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Jing took Xiangyang without looting and calmed the populace.

sentences.zh: 晉平北將軍魏該弟遐等率該部眾自石城降於敬。

translations.literal: Jin’s General Who Pacifies the North Wei Gai’s younger brother Xia and others led Gai’s host from Shicheng to surrender to Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Xia, brother of Jin’s northern pacifier Wei Gai, led Wei’s troops from Shicheng over to Guo Jing.

sentences.zh: 敬毀襄陽，遷其百姓于沔北，城樊城以戍之。

translations.literal: Jing destroyed Xiangyang, moved its common people north of the Mian, and walled Fancheng to garrison them.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Jing razed Xiangyang, deported the people north of the Han, and fortified Fancheng as their new home.

sentences.zh: 秦州休屠王羌叛于勒，刺史臨深遣司馬管光帥州軍討之，為羌所敗，隴右大擾，氐羌悉叛。

translations.literal: In Qinzhou the Xiutu king of the Qiang, Wang Qiang, rebelled against Le; Inspector Lin Shen sent Marshal Guan Guang to lead provincial troops against him, was defeated by Qiang, Longyou was greatly disturbed, and Di and Qiang all rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: The Xiutu Qiang chief Wang Qiang rose in Qinzhou; governor Lin Shen’s marshal Guan Guang lost, the Long salient erupted, and every Di and Qiang clan mutinied.

sentences.zh: 勒遣石生進據隴城。

translations.literal: Le sent Shi Sheng to advance and occupy Longcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le sent Shi Sheng to seize Longcheng.

sentences.zh: 王羌兄子擢與羌有仇，生乃賂擢，與掎擊之。

translations.literal: Wang Qiang’s elder brother’s son Zhuo bore a grudge against Qiang; Sheng thereupon bribed Zhuo and with him pincer-attacked Qiang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhuo, Wang Qiang’s nephew, hated his uncle; Shi Sheng bought him and coordinated a two-pronged strike.

sentences.zh: 羌敗，奔涼州。

translations.literal: Qiang was defeated and fled to Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qiang broke and ran for Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 徙秦州夷豪五千餘戶於雍州。

translations.literal: He moved over five thousand households of Qinzhou Yi chieftains to Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He deported five thousand Qinzhou tribal headmen’s households into Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 勒下書曰：「自今諸有處法，悉依科令。

translations.literal: Le issued documents: “From now on, wherever punishments are applied, wholly follow the statutes and ordinances.
translations.idiomatic: He announced: “Justice must follow the written code.

sentences.zh: 吾所忿戮、怒發中旨者，若德位已高，不宜訓罰，或服勤死事之孤，邂逅罹譴，門下皆各列奏之，吾當思擇而行也。

translations.literal: Where I in wrath execute or in anger issue a mid-palace order, if virtue and rank are already high and they ought not receive instruction by punishment, or if they are orphans of those who died in diligent service to the state and by chance meet reproach, let each office under the gate list and memorialize—I shall think and choose how to act.”
translations.idiomatic: If my temper strikes the wrong man—someone of high virtue or a war orphan—the gate offices must appeal before I carry it out.”

sentences.zh: 」堂陽人陳豬妻一產三男，賜其衣帛廩食，乳婢一口，復三歲勿事。

translations.literal: ” A Tangyang man, Chen Zhu’s wife, in one birth bore three boys; he bestowed on her clothes, silk, granary rations, one wet-nurse slave, and exempted her three years from labor service.
translations.idiomatic: ” A Tangyang woman bore triplets; Shi Le sent cloth, grain, a nursemaid, and three years’ tax relief.

sentences.zh: 時高句麗、肅慎致其楛矢，宇文屋孤並獻名馬於勒。

translations.literal: At the time Gaogouli and Sushen sent their mulberry-arrow shafts, and Wuyuwugu together presented famous horses to Le.
translations.idiomatic: Koguryŏ and Sushen sent ritual arrows; the Wuyuwugu tribe added fine horses.

sentences.zh: 涼州牧張駿遣長史馬詵奉圖送高昌、于闐、鄯善、大宛使，獻其方物。

translations.literal: Liangzhou Shepherd Zhang Jun sent chief clerk Ma Shen to present maps and deliver envoys of Gaochang, Khotan, Shanshan, and Ferghana, presenting their local products.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun’s chief clerk Ma Shen brought maps and embassies from Gaochang, Khotan, Shanshan, and Ferghana with their gifts.

sentences.zh: 晉荊州牧陶侃遣兼長史王敷聘於勒，致江南之珍寶奇獸。

translations.literal: Jin’s Jingzhou shepherd Tao Kan sent concurrent chief clerk Wang Fu on a mission to Le, delivering south-of-the-River treasures and strange beasts.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan of Jin dispatched Wang Fu with southern curios and rare animals.

sentences.zh: 秦州送白獸、白鹿，荊州送白雉、白兔，濟陰木連理，甘露降苑鄉。

translations.literal: Qinzhou sent white beasts and white deer; Jingzhou sent white pheasants and white rabbits; Jiyin had interlocking trees; sweet dew fell at Yuanxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Qinzhou offered white deer and beasts, Jingzhou white pheasants and hares, Jiyin reported grafted trees, and sweet dew fell on Yuanxiang.

sentences.zh: 勒以休瑞並臻，遐方慕義，赦三歲刑已下，均百姓去年逋調；

translations.literal: Le, because felicitous omens arrived together and distant regions admired righteousness, amnestied crimes up to three years’ labor, and averaged out the common people’s overdue levies of the previous year;
translations.idiomatic: Citing the flood of omens and foreign goodwill, he remitted light sentences and wrote off last year’s back taxes;

sentences.zh: 特赦涼州殊死，涼州計吏皆拜郎中，賜絹十匹，綿十斤。

translations.literal: he specially amnestied capital crimes in Liangzhou, and for Liangzhou clerks on annual duty each appointed them gentlemen of the palace, bestowing ten bolts of silk and ten jin of floss each.
translations.idiomatic: he spared capital crimes in Liangzhou, named every Liangzhou clerk-reporter a gentleman of the palace, and gave each ten bolts of silk and ten jin of floss.

sentences.zh: 勒南郊，有白氣自壇屬天，勒大悅，還宮，赦四歲刑。

translations.literal: Le at the southern suburban altar had white vapor run from the altar to Heaven; Le was greatly pleased, returned to the palace, and amnestied crimes up to four years’ labor.
translations.idiomatic: At the southern altar a white beam rose to the sky; Shi Le, elated, amnestied sentences up to four years.

sentences.zh: 遣使封張駿武威郡公，食涼州諸郡。

translations.literal: He sent envoys to enfeoff Zhang Jun as Duke of Wuwei commandery, feeding on all Liangzhou commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: He enfeoffed Zhang Jun duke of Wuwei with income from every Liangzhou county.

sentences.zh: 勒親耕藉田，還宮，赦五歲刑，賜其公卿已下金帛有差。

translations.literal: Le personally plowed the sacred field, returned to the palace, amnestied crimes up to five years’ labor, and bestowed gold and silk on dukes and ministers downward in graded amounts.
translations.idiomatic: After plowing the ritual field he freed convicts up to five years’ labor and showered gold and silk on the bureaucracy.

sentences.zh: 勒以日蝕，避正殿三日，令群公卿士各上封事。

translations.literal: Le, because of a solar eclipse, avoided the main hall three days and ordered dukes and ministers each to submit sealed memorials.
translations.idiomatic: An eclipse sent him from court for three days and brought a call for sealed advice.

sentences.zh: 禁州郡諸祠堂非正典者皆除之，其能興雲致雨，有益於百姓者，郡縣更為立祠堂，殖嘉樹，准嶽瀆已下為差等。

translations.literal: He forbade province and commandery shrines not in the orthodox canon, all to be removed; where they could raise clouds and bring rain and benefit the hundred surnames, let commanderies and counties instead erect shrines for them, planting fine trees, with graded ranks below the marchmounts and rivers.
translations.idiomatic: He tore down uncanonical shrines but ordered useful rain shrines rebuilt with fine trees, ranked below the great river and mountain cults.

sentences.zh: 勒將營鄴宮，廷尉續咸上書切諫。

translations.literal: Le was about to build the Ye palaces when Commandant of Justice Xu Xian submitted a memorial sharply remonstrating.
translations.idiomatic: When he resumed the Ye palace project, commandant Xu Xian sent a blistering memorial.

sentences.zh: 勒大怒，曰：「不斬此老臣。

translations.literal: Le was greatly angry and said, “If I do not behead this old minister,
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le roared, “Unless I kill this old fool,

sentences.zh: 朕宮不得成也！

translations.literal: my palace cannot be completed!”
translations.idiomatic: my palace will never rise!”

sentences.zh: 」敕御史收之。

translations.literal: ” He ordered the imperial clerk to seize him.
translations.idiomatic: ” and ordered the censor to arrest him.

sentences.zh: 中書令徐光進曰：「陛下天資聰睿，超邁唐虞，而更不欲聞忠臣之言，豈夏癸、商辛之君邪？

translations.literal: Palace Secretary Xu Guang stepped forward and said, “Your Majesty’s Heaven-given nature is keen and wise, surpassing Tang and Yu, yet further you do not wish to hear loyal ministers’ words—are you a lord like Xia Jie or King Zhou of Shang?
translations.idiomatic: Xu Guang intervened: “You surpass Yao and Shun—must you mimic Jie and the last king of Shang?

sentences.zh: 其言可用用之，不可用故當容之，奈何一旦以直言而斬列卿乎！

translations.literal: If the words can be used, use them; if they cannot be used, still you ought to tolerate them—how in one morning because of straight words behead a ranked minister!”
translations.idiomatic: Use good advice or set it aside, but do not behead a minister for bluntness!”

sentences.zh: 」勒歎曰：「為人君不得自專如是！

translations.literal: ” Le sighed and said, “To be lord of men and not get to decide on one’s own like this!
translations.idiomatic: ” Shi Le sighed: “So an emperor cannot even bluster in peace!

sentences.zh: 豈不識此言之忠乎？

translations.literal: Did I not recognize this speech’s loyalty?”
translations.idiomatic: Did I miss how loyal he was?”

sentences.zh: 向戲之爾。

translations.literal: ” “Earlier I was only jesting.”
translations.idiomatic: ” “I was only joking.”

sentences.zh: 人家有百匹資，尚欲市別宅，況有天下之富，萬乘之尊乎！

translations.literal: When a household has a hundred bolts of wealth, it still wishes to buy another mansion—how much more when there is the wealth of the world and the honor of the ten thousand chariots!”
translations.idiomatic: A family with a hundred bolts still buys a second house—why should an emperor stint?”

sentences.zh: 終當繕之耳。

translations.literal: ” “In the end I shall repair it.”
translations.idiomatic: ” “I will build it yet.”

sentences.zh: 且敕停作，成吾直臣之氣也。

translations.literal: ” “For now order construction stopped, completing my straight minister’s integrity.”
translations.idiomatic: ” “Hold the work and honor his integrity instead.”

sentences.zh: 」因賜咸絹百匹，稻百斛。

translations.literal: ” Thereupon he bestowed on Xu Xian one hundred bolts of silk and one hundred hu of rice.
translations.idiomatic: ” He then gave Xu Xian a hundred bolts of silk and a hundred hu of rice.

sentences.zh: 又下書令公卿百僚歲薦賢良、方正、直言、秀異、至孝、廉清各一人，答策上第者拜議郎，中第中郎，下第郎中。

translations.literal: Again he issued documents ordering dukes and ministers of a hundred offices annually to recommend one man each among worthy and good, upright and correct, outspoken, outstanding, supreme filial, and incorrupt and pure; those who answered policy questions in the highest grade were appointed advisers to the deliberations, middle grade gentlemen of the palace, lower grade gentlemen of the palace.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered yearly nominations of worthies, each category one man, with policy-test scores fixing whether they became deliberation advisers, palace gentlemen upper or middle grade.

sentences.zh: 其舉人得遞相薦引，廣招賢之路。

translations.literal: Those recommended might in turn recommend one another, widening the road to worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Nominees could chain-recommend others to widen the talent net.

sentences.zh: 起明堂、辟雍、靈台于襄國城西。

translations.literal: He raised the Bright Hall, Biyong, and Spirit Terrace west of Xiangguo city.
translations.idiomatic: He broke ground for the Bright Hall, imperial academy moat, and observatory west of Xiangguo.

sentences.zh: 時大雨霖，中山西北暴水，流漂巨木百餘萬根，集于堂陽。

translations.literal: At the time great rains fell in long spells; northwest of Zhongshan a violent flood floated and drifted over a million great logs, gathering at Tangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Monsoon floods northwest of Zhongshan swept a million logs down to Tangyang.

sentences.zh: 勒大悅，謂公卿曰：「諸卿知不？

translations.literal: Le was greatly pleased and said to the dukes and ministers, “Do you gentlemen know?
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le asked his court, “Do you see?

sentences.zh: 此非為災也，天意欲吾營鄴都耳。

translations.literal: This is not a disaster—Heaven’s intent is that I should build the Ye capital.”
translations.idiomatic: This is no calamity—Heaven is shipping timber for Ye.”

sentences.zh: 」於是令少府任汪、都水使者張漸等監營鄴宮，勒親授規模。

translations.literal: ” Thereupon he ordered Junior Masters Ren Wang, waterworks envoy Zhang Jian, and others to supervise building the Ye palaces, and Le personally handed down the layout.
translations.idiomatic: ” He put Ren Wang and Zhang Jian in charge of Ye’s construction and sketched the plan himself.

sentences.zh: 蜀梓潼、建平、漢固三郡蠻巴降於勒。

translations.literal: The Man-Ba of Shu’s Zitong, Jianping, and Hangu three commanderies surrendered to Le.
translations.idiomatic: The Ba tribes of Zitong, Jianping, and Hangu in Shu submitted to him.

sentences.zh: 勒以成周土中，漢晉舊京，復欲有移都之意，乃命洛陽為南都，置行台治書侍御史于洛陽。

translations.literal: Le, because Chengzhou lay in the middle of the earth as the old capital of Han and Jin, again wished to move the capital; he therefore ordered Luoyang to be the southern capital and set up a mobile headquarters clerk of the masters of writing at Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Deeming Luoyang the ancient heart of Han and Jin, he named it southern capital and posted a mobile secretariat there.

sentences.zh: 勒因饗高句麗、宇文屋孤使，酒酣，謂徐光曰：「朕方自古開基何等主也？

translations.literal: Le, because he feasted envoys of Gaogouli and Wuyuwugu, when the wine ran high said to Xu Guang, “I, compared with founders of antiquity, what manner of lord am I?
translations.idiomatic: Feasting Koguryŏ and Wuyuwugu envoys, he asked Xu Guang drunk: “How do I rank among the founders of old?”

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「陛下神武籌略邁于高皇，雄藝卓犖超絕魏祖，自三王已來無可比也，其軒轅之亞乎！

translations.literal: ” He replied, “Your Majesty’s divine martial planning surpasses the Exalted Founder’s, your heroic arts tower above Wei’s progenitor; since the Three Kings there has been none to compare—perhaps he is next after the Yellow Lord!”
translations.idiomatic: ” Xu Guang answered: “Your might and design outstrip Gaozu of Han, your brilliance tops Cao Cao—since the Three Kings none rival you; perhaps only the Yellow Emperor stands above.”

sentences.zh: 」勒笑曰：「人豈不自知，卿言亦乙太過。

translations.literal: ” Le laughed and said, “How could a man not know himself—your words are also somewhat too much.
translations.idiomatic: ” Shi Le laughed: “A man should know himself—flattery that strong overshoots the mark.

sentences.zh: 朕若逢高皇，當北面而事之，與韓彭競鞭而爭先耳。

translations.literal: If I met the Exalted Founder, I would serve him facing north, and with Han and Peng vie with whip to be first.”
translations.idiomatic: Face to face with Han Gaozu I would serve him as vassal and only race Han Xin and Peng Yue for second place.”

sentences.zh: 脫遇光武，當並驅于中原，未知鹿死誰手。

translations.literal: If I chanced to meet Guangwu, we would gallop side by side in the Central Plain, and it would not be known on whose hand the deer would die.
translations.idiomatic: Against Guangwu I would match him stroke for stroke in the heartland—who bags the deer would be anyone’s guess.”

sentences.zh: 大丈夫行事當礌礌落落，如日月皎然，終不能如曹孟德、司馬仲達父子，欺他孤兒寡婦，狐媚以取天下也。

translations.literal: A great man’s conduct ought to be open and straight, bright as sun and moon; in the end one cannot be like Cao Mengde and Sima Zhongda father and son, bullying orphan boys and widowed mothers with foxy charm to seize the realm.”
translations.idiomatic: Great men move like sunlight—never like Cao Cao or the Simas, who foxed widows and orphans into an empire.”

sentences.zh: 朕當在二劉之間耳，軒轅豈所擬乎！

translations.literal: I ought to stand between the two Lius; how could the Yellow Lord be what I match!”
translations.idiomatic: I belong between the two Lius; the Yellow Emperor is no measure for me!”

sentences.zh: 」其群臣皆頓首稱萬歲。

translations.literal: ” His host of ministers all knocked their heads and shouted “Ten thousand years!”
translations.idiomatic: ” The courtiers kowtowed and shouted long life.

sentences.zh: 晉將軍趙胤攻克馬頭，石堪遣將軍韓雍救之，至則無及，遂寇南沙、海虞，俘獲五千餘人。

translations.literal: Jin General Zhao Yin stormed and took Matou; Shi Kan sent General Han Yong to rescue, but when he arrived it was too late, so he raided Nansha and Haiyu and captured over five thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yin took Matou before Han Yong arrived; Shi Kan’s relief column veered to raid Nansha and Haiyu and bagged five thousand captives instead.

sentences.zh: 初，郭敬之退據樊城也，王師復戍襄陽。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Guo Jing had withdrawn to hold Fancheng, the royal army again garrisoned Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: After Guo Jing fell back to Fancheng, Jin had reoccupied Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 至是，敬又攻陷之，留戍而歸。

translations.literal: At this point Jing again stormed and took it, left a garrison, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Now Guo Jing retook it, posted a garrison, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 暴風大雨，震電建德殿端門、襄國市西門，殺五人。

translations.literal: Violent wind and great rain; lightning struck Jiande Hall’s front gate and Xiangguo market’s west gate, killing five men.
translations.idiomatic: A squall shattered the Jiande gate and the west gate of Xiangguo market, killing five.

sentences.zh: 雹起西河介山，大如雞子，平地三尺，洿下丈餘，行人禽獸死者萬數，曆太原、樂平、武鄉、趙郡、廣平、钜鹿千餘里，樹木摧折，禾稼蕩然。

translations.literal: Hail arose west of the River at Jie Mountain, large as chicken eggs, three chi deep on the flat and more than a zhang in low ground; travelers and birds and beasts dead numbered in the myriads; it passed through Taiyuan, Leping, Wuxiang, Zhao, Guangping, and Julu for over a thousand li, trees snapped, crops utterly flattened.
translations.idiomatic: Hailstones egg-sized fell from Jie Mountain west of the river, piling three feet deep and drowning low ground; corpses of men and beasts littered a thousand li from Taiyuan through Julu, forests stripped and fields erased.

sentences.zh: 勒正服於東堂，以問徐光曰：「歷代已來有斯災幾也？

translations.literal: Le in full dress at the eastern hall asked Xu Guang, “Since successive dynasties, how many times has there been such a disaster?”
translations.idiomatic: In court robes at the eastern hall he asked Xu Guang how often history had seen a calamity like this.

sentences.zh: 」光對曰：「周、漢、魏、晉皆有之，雖天地之常事，然明主未始不為變，所以敬天之怒也。

translations.literal: ” Guang replied, “Zhou, Han, Wei, and Jin all had them; though they are Heaven and Earth’s regular events, yet enlightened lords never fail to treat them as portents—thereby respecting Heaven’s anger.”
translations.idiomatic: ” Xu Guang said every dynasty had seen such omens; wise rulers always took them as Heaven’s rebuke.

sentences.zh: 去年禁寒食，介推，帝鄉之神也，歷代所尊，或者以為未宜替也。

translations.literal: Last year you banned Cold Food; Jie Tui is a god of the imperial domain, honored by every generation—some perhaps thought it should not have been abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Last year you banned the Cold Food festival; Jie Zitui is a tutelary hero—many thought ending his rite unwise.

sentences.zh: 一人籲嗟，王道尚為之虧，況群神怨憾而不怒動上帝乎！

translations.literal: One man’s sigh, and the kingly way still suffers loss for it—how much more when host of spirits harbor resentment and do not move the Lord on High to anger!”
translations.idiomatic: A single cry can dent the kingly way—what of countless angry gods shaking Heaven?”

sentences.zh: 縱不能令天下同爾，介山左右，晉文之所封也，宜任百姓奉之。

translations.literal: Even if you cannot make the realm uniform in this, the lands around Jie Mountain were enfeoffed by Duke Wen of Jin—let the common people there serve him.”
translations.idiomatic: If you cannot please everyone, at least let the people of Mian and Jie keep honoring Jie Zitui, as Duke Wen once enfeoffed that ground.”

sentences.zh: 」勒下書曰：「寒食既并州之舊風，朕生其俗，不能異也。

translations.literal: ” Le issued documents: “Cold Food is Bingzhou’s old custom; I was born to that folk and cannot differ from them.
translations.idiomatic: ” Shi Le decreed: “Cold Food is Bingzhou’s custom; I was born there and will not forbid it outright.

sentences.zh: 前者外議以子推諸侯之臣，王者不應為忌，故從其議，倘或由之而致斯災乎！

translations.literal: Earlier outsiders debated that, because Zitui was a feudatory minister, a king ought not observe taboo for him, so I followed their debate—perhaps thereby this disaster was brought about!”
translations.idiomatic: Counselors said a king need not mourn a subject like Jie Zitui, so I lifted the ban—maybe that invited this storm!”

sentences.zh: 子推雖朕鄉之神，非法食者亦不得亂也，尚書其促檢舊典定議以聞。

translations.literal: Although Zitui is my homeland’s god, those who eat contrary to prohibition must not be disorderly either—let the masters of writing hasten to inspect old canons, fix a decision, and report.”
translations.idiomatic: He remains our local god, yet lawless feasting must stop—have the secretariat dig precedent and report.”

sentences.zh: 」有司奏以子推歷代攸尊，請普復寒食，更為植嘉樹，立祠堂，給戶奉祀。

translations.literal: ” The offices memorialized that, because Zitui had been honored through the ages, they asked universally to restore Cold Food, again plant fine trees, erect shrines, and assign households for sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Officials answered: restore Cold Food empire-wide for Jie Zitui, replant groves, rebuild shrines, and fund custodian households.

sentences.zh: 勒黃門郎韋謏駁曰：「案《春秋》，藏冰失道，陰氣發洩為雹。

translations.literal: Le’s Yellow Gate Gentleman Wei Sou refuted: “According to the Spring and Autumn Annals, when stored ice misses the proper way, yin qi vents forth as hail.
translations.idiomatic: Huangmen Wei Sou cited the Chunqiu: mis-stored ice releases yin and falls as hail.

sentences.zh: 自子推已前，雹者復何所致？

translations.literal: Before Zitui, when there was hail, what caused it?
translations.idiomatic: What caused hail before Jie Zitui ever lived?

sentences.zh: 此自陰陽乖錯所為耳。

translations.literal: This comes from yin and yang’s mutual disorder—that is all.
translations.idiomatic: It is yin and yang out of joint—nothing more.

sentences.zh: 且子推賢者，曷為暴害如此！

translations.literal: Moreover Zitui was a worthy—how could he violently harm like this!
translations.idiomatic: Jie Zitui was a sage—would he slaughter thousands in spite?

sentences.zh: 求之冥趣，必不然矣。

translations.literal: Seeking it in hidden causes, assuredly it is not so.
translations.idiomatic: Probe the unseen: that cannot be his doing.

sentences.zh: 今雖為冰室，懼所藏之冰不在固陰沍寒之地，多皆山川之側，氣泄為雹也。

translations.literal: Now although there are ice chambers, I fear the stored ice is not in places of solid yin and frozen cold—mostly beside mountains and rivers where qi leaks and becomes hail.
translations.idiomatic: Our ice houses may sit too warm; ice stacked near warm valleys vents qi and seeds hail.

sentences.zh: 以子推忠賢，令綿、介之間奉之為允，於天下則不通矣。

translations.literal: To order Mian and Jie’s region alone to honor Zitui as a loyal worthy is fitting; toward the whole realm it would not be consistent.”
translations.idiomatic: Let Mian and Jie alone honor him; a universal cult would not wash.”

sentences.zh: 」勒從之。

translations.literal: ” Le followed this.
translations.idiomatic: ” Shi Le accepted Wei Sou’s view.

sentences.zh: 於是遷冰室于重陰凝寒之所，并州復寒食如初。

translations.literal: Thereupon they moved the ice chamber to a place of heavy yin and congealed cold, and Bingzhou restored Cold Food as at first.
translations.idiomatic: They relocated the royal ice vault to deep shade and reauthorized Cold Food in Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 勒令其太子省可尚書奏事，使中常侍嚴震參綜可否，征伐刑斷大事乃呈之。

translations.literal: Le ordered his crown prince to review and approve the masters of writing’s memorials, had palace attendant Yan Zhen join in judging what was acceptable, and only for great matters of campaign, punishment, or execution presented them.
translations.idiomatic: He had Crown Prince Shi Hong vet memorials with eunuch Yan Zhen; only wars and executions reached his sickbed.

sentences.zh: 自是震威權之盛過於主相矣。

translations.literal: From this Zhen’s awesomeness and authority’s greatness surpassed the chief ministers’.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zhen’s power soon eclipsed the chief ministers’.

sentences.zh: 季龍之門可設雀羅，季龍愈怏怏不悅。

translations.literal: At Tigun’s gate one could set a sparrow net; Tigun grew ever more sullen and displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu’s gate grew so quiet you could catch sparrows there; he brooded in resentment.

sentences.zh: 郭敬南掠江西，晉南中郎將桓宣承其虛攻樊城，取城中之眾而去。

translations.literal: Guo Jing raided south of the River west; Jin’s South Leader of Court Gentlemen Huan Xuan exploited his emptiness to attack Fancheng, taking the host within the city and leaving.
translations.idiomatic: While Guo Jing raided Jiangxi, Huan Xuan slipped into empty Fancheng and marched its garrison away.

sentences.zh: 敬旋師救樊，追戰于涅水。

translations.literal: Jing wheeled the army to rescue Fancheng and pursued battle at the Nie River.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Jing doubled back and caught Huan Xuan at the Nie River.

sentences.zh: 敬前軍大敗，宣亦死傷太半，盡取所掠而止。

translations.literal: Jing’s van was heavily defeated; Xuan likewise lost more than half dead and wounded, and only stopped when he had recovered all that had been plundered.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Jing’s van lost heavily, yet Huan Xuan lost half his men before abandoning the loot and fleeing.

sentences.zh: 宣遂南取襄陽，留軍戍之。

translations.literal: Xuan thereupon took Xiangyang southward and left troops to garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan then drove south into Xiangyang and left a garrison.

sentences.zh: 勒如鄴，臨石季龍第，謂之曰：「功力不可並興，待宮殿成後，當為王起第，勿以卑小悒悒也。

translations.literal: Le went to Ye, visited Shi Tigun’s mansion, and said to him, “Labor power cannot be raised on two fronts at once; after palaces are finished, I shall raise a mansion for the king—do not be depressed over being low and small.
translations.idiomatic: Visiting Shi Hu in Ye, Shi Le said: “Finish my palace first, then yours—do not sulk at cramped quarters.

sentences.zh: 」季龍免冠拜謝，勒曰：「與王共有天下，何所謝也！

translations.literal: ” Tigun doffed cap and thanked him; Le said, “With the king I share the realm—what is there to thank!”
translations.idiomatic: ” Shi Hu kowtowed thanks until Shi Le said they shared the empire—no thanks needed.”

sentences.zh: 」有流星大如象，尾足蛇形，自北極西南流五十餘丈，光明燭地，墜於河，聲聞九百餘里。

translations.literal: ” There was a meteor as large as an elephant, tail and feet like a serpent’s shape, flowing from the north pole southwest fifty-plus zhang, its light candle-bright on the earth; it fell into the River, and the sound was heard over nine hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: ” A meteor elephant-sized, serpent-tailed, streaked fifty yards from the pole toward the southwest, lit the ground like noon, splashed into the Yellow River with a boom heard three hundred miles away.

sentences.zh: 黑龍見鄴井中，勒觀龍有喜色。

translations.literal: A black dragon appeared in a Ye well; Le, viewing the dragon, had a pleased expression.
translations.idiomatic: A black dragon rose from a Ye well; Shi Le smiled at the omen.

sentences.zh: 朝其群臣於鄴。

translations.literal: He held court for his host of ministers at Ye.
translations.idiomatic: He held audience at Ye.

sentences.zh: 命郡國立學官，每郡置博士祭酒二人，弟子百五十人，三考修成，顯升台府。

translations.literal: He ordered commanderies and principalities to establish school officers, each commandery to set two erudite libationers and one hundred fifty disciples, with three examinations to completion, then conspicuous promotion to the terrace offices.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered every commandery to open schools—two erudites, a hundred fifty students, three exams, then promotion to central posts.

sentences.zh: 於是擢拜太學生五人為佐著作郎，錄述時事。

translations.literal: Thereupon he promoted five Imperial University students to assistant editorial directors to record the times’ affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Five imperial students became assistant compilers to chronicle current events.

sentences.zh: 時大旱，勒親臨廷尉錄囚徒，五歲刑已下皆輕決遣之，重者賜酒食，聽沐浴，一須秋論。

translations.literal: At the time there was great drought; Le personally went to the commandant of justice to review prisoners: those with labor sentences up through five years he lightly judged and released; the heavy cases he granted wine and food, allowed bathing, to await autumn judgment.
translations.idiomatic: In drought he sat in the commandant’s jail, paroled minor convicts, and postponed capital cases until autumn.

sentences.zh: 還未及宮，澍雨大降。

translations.literal: Before he had returned to the palace, soaking rain fell in great volume.
translations.idiomatic: Before he reached the palace a soaking rain fell.

sentences.zh: 勒如其灃水宮，因疾甚而還。

translations.literal: Le went to his Fen River palace and, because his illness was severe, returned.
translations.idiomatic: He visited his lodge on the Fen River, then turned back as his illness worsened.

sentences.zh: 召石季龍與其太子弘、中常侍嚴震等待疾禁中。

translations.literal: He summoned Shi Tigun, his crown prince Hong, palace attendant Yan Zhen, and others to attend his illness within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: He called Shi Hu, crown prince Shi Hong, Yan Zhen, and others to his bedside.

sentences.zh: 季龍矯命絕弘、震及內外群臣親戚，勒疾之增損莫有知者。

translations.literal: Tigun forged orders cutting off Hong, Zhen, and inner and outer ministers and kin; none knew the waxing and waning of Le’s illness.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu forged edicts isolating Shi Hong, Yan Zhen, and the court from Shi Le’s sickroom—no one knew whether the emperor improved or failed.

sentences.zh: 詐召石宏、石堪還襄國。

translations.literal: He falsely summoned Shi Hong (the Prince of Qin) and Shi Kan back to Xiangguo.
translations.idiomatic: He forged an edict recalling Prince of Qin Shi Hong and Shi Kan to Xiangguo.

sentences.zh: 勒疾小瘳，見宏，驚曰：「秦王何故來邪？

translations.literal: Le’s illness slightly improved; seeing Hong, he said in alarm, “Why has the Prince of Qin come?
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Le briefly rallied and saw Shi Hong, he cried, “Why is the Prince of Qin here?”

sentences.zh: 使王籓鎮，正備今日。

translations.literal: I ordered princely garrisons precisely to guard against this day.
translations.idiomatic: I posted you princes on the marches for exactly this contingency.”

sentences.zh: 有呼者邪？

translations.literal: Was there one who summoned you?
translations.idiomatic: Did someone summon you?”

sentences.zh: 自來也？

translations.literal: Did you come of yourself?
translations.idiomatic: Or did you come on your own?”

sentences.zh: 有呼者誅之！

translations.literal: If there was one who summoned you, execute him!”
translations.idiomatic: Whoever called you here dies.”

sentences.zh: 」季龍大懼曰：「秦王思慕暫還耳，今謹遣之。

translations.literal: ” Tigun was greatly frightened and said, “The Prince of Qin missed you and returned briefly; now I respectfully send him off.”
translations.idiomatic: ” Shi Hu stammered that the prince had missed his father and would leave at once.”

sentences.zh: 」數日復問之，季龍曰：「奉詔即遣，今已半路矣。

translations.literal: ” Several days later he asked again; Tigun said, “We obeyed the edict and sent him off; now he is already halfway.”
translations.idiomatic: ” Days later Shi Le asked again; Shi Hu claimed the prince was already halfway home.”

sentences.zh: 」更諭宏在外，遂不遣之。

translations.literal: ” He further instructed Hong to stay outside, and in the end did not dispatch him.
translations.idiomatic: ” He kept Shi Hong outside the capital and never let him return to his command.

sentences.zh: 廣阿蝗。

translations.literal: Locusts at Guang’a.
translations.idiomatic: Locusts swarmed Guang’a.

sentences.zh: 季龍密遣其子邃率騎三千游於蝗所。

translations.literal: Tigun secretly sent his son Sui leading three thousand horse to roam where the locusts were.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu secretly sent Shi Sui with three thousand riders to “patrol” the swarm.

sentences.zh: 熒惑人昴。

translations.literal: The Fire Star entered the Mao asterism.
translations.idiomatic: Mars trespassed into the Pleiades.

sentences.zh: 星隕于鄴東北六十里，初赤黑黃雲如幕，長數十匹，交錯，聲如雷震，墜地氣熱如火，塵起連天。

translations.literal: A star fell sixty li northeast of Ye; at first red-black-yellow clouds like a curtain, several tens of bolts long, interwoven, sound like thunderclaps; when it struck earth the qi was hot as fire, dust rose linking sky.
translations.idiomatic: A meteor hit sixty li northeast of Ye, preceded by tricolor clouds, thunder, scorching wind, and dust pillars.

sentences.zh: 時有耕者往視之，土猶燃沸，見有一石方尺餘，青色而輕，擊之間聲如磬。

translations.literal: At the time a plowman went to look; the earth still boiled with heat; he saw a stone just over a chi square, bluish and light; striking it, between-strikes sound like a chime-stone.
translations.idiomatic: A farmer found the crater still boiling and a light blue foot-square stone that rang like a bell when struck.

sentences.zh: 勒疾甚，遺令：「三日而葬，內外百僚既葬除服，無禁婚娶、祭祀、飲酒、食肉，征鎮牧守不得輒離所司以奔喪，斂以時服，載以常車，無藏金寶，無內器玩。

translations.literal: Le was gravely ill and left testament: “Bury after three days; inner and outer hundred officials, once buried, remove mourning—do not forbid marriage, sacrifice, drinking, or eating meat; expedition and garrison shepherds and guards must not rashly leave their posts to rush mourning; enfold in timely dress, carry on ordinary carts, do not bury gold or jewels, do not place vessels or playthings within.”
translations.idiomatic: His will demanded a three-day funeral, quick release from mourning, no ban on weddings or wine, no recall of frontier generals, plain shrouds and carts, no grave goods.

sentences.zh: 大雅沖幼，恐非能構荷朕志。

translations.literal: Daya is young and tender—I fear he cannot shoulder and carry out my intent.
translations.idiomatic: Daya (Shi Hong) is too young to shoulder my design.

sentences.zh: 中山已下其各司所典，無違朕命。

translations.literal: From the Prince of Zhongshan downward, let each manage what his office holds—do not disobey my command.
translations.idiomatic: From Shi Hu downward every minister must keep his post—obey my word.

sentences.zh: 大雅與斌宜善相維持，司馬氏汝等之殷鑒，其務于敦穆也。

translations.literal: Daya and Bin ought well mutually to support each other; the Sima clan is your bronze mirror—strive for thick harmony.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hong and Shi Bin must stand together; take the Simas as your warning and keep the peace.

sentences.zh: 中山王深可三思周霍，勿為將來口實。

translations.literal: The Prince of Zhongshan should deeply thrice ponder Zhou and Huo—do not become a handle for later mouths.”
translations.idiomatic: Let Zhongshan king Shi Hu think thrice of the Han regents Zhou and Huo—give posterity no excuse.”

sentences.zh: 」以咸和七年死，時年六十，在位十五年。

translations.literal: ” In the seventh year of Xianhe he died, age sixty, having occupied the throne fifteen years.
translations.idiomatic: ” He died in Xianhe 7 at sixty after fifteen years on the throne.

sentences.zh: 夜瘞山谷，莫知其所，備文物虛葬，號高平陵。

translations.literal: By night they buried him in a mountain valley, none knowing the place; they prepared full ritual gear for a false burial, titled Gaoping tumulus.
translations.idiomatic: His corpse was slipped into a secret valley; a dummy mausoleum named Gaoling received the state regalia.

sentences.zh: 偽諡明皇帝，廟號高祖。

translations.literal: They falsely posthumously titled him Brilliant Emperor, temple name Exalted Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: He received the false posthumous title Ming emperor and temple name Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 弘字大雅，勒之第二子也。

translations.literal: Hong’s style was Daya; he was Le’s second son.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hong, courtesy Daya, was Shi Le’s second son.

sentences.zh: 幼有孝行，以恭謙自守，受經于杜嘏，誦律于續咸。

translations.literal: In youth he had filial conduct, guarded himself with respectful modesty, received the classics from Du Jia, and recited statutes from Xu Xian.
translations.idiomatic: He was dutiful, modest, studied the Classics under Du Jia and law under Xu Xian.

sentences.zh: 勒曰：「今世非承平，不可專以文業教也。

translations.literal: Le said, “The present age is not one of full peace; one cannot teach exclusively with literary pursuits.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le said: “These are not peaceful times—book learning alone will not do.

sentences.zh: 」於是使劉征、任播授以兵書，王陽教之擊刺。

translations.literal: ” Thereupon he had Liu Zheng and Ren Bo give him military treatises, and Wang Yang teach him thrusting and stabbing.
translations.idiomatic: ” He set Liu Zheng and Ren Bo to teach war manuals and Wang Yang to drill spear work.

sentences.zh: 立為世子，領中領軍，尋暑衛將軍，使領開府辟召，後鎮鄴。

translations.literal: He was established as heir apparent, heading the central palace guard; soon he was appointed General Who Guards the Court, ordered to head document recruitment with independent command, later garrisoned Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Named heir and central guard commander, soon palace guard general with independent recruitment, later posted to Ye.

sentences.zh: 勒僭位，立為太子。

translations.literal: When Le usurped the throne, he was established crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Le took the imperial style, Shi Hong became crown prince.

sentences.zh: 虛襟愛士，好為文詠，其所親昵，莫非儒素。

translations.literal: He emptied his bosom to love scholars, loved to compose literary pieces; those he drew near were none who were not Confucian and plain.
translations.idiomatic: He courted literati, wrote poetry, and befriended only scholars.

sentences.zh: 勒謂徐光曰：「大雅愔愔，殊不似將家子。

translations.literal: Le said to Xu Guang, “Daya is gentle and mild—he utterly does not resemble a general’s house son.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le told Xu Guang: “Daya is all gentleness—hardly a warrior’s son.

sentences.zh: 」光曰：「漢祖以馬上取天下，孝文以玄默守之，聖人之後，必世勝殘，天之道也。

translations.literal: ” Guang said, “Han’s founder took the realm on horseback; filial Wen guarded it in dark silence; after a sage, a generation must overcome cruelty—this is Heaven’s way.”
translations.idiomatic: ” Xu Guang replied: “Gaozu conquered from the saddle; Wenjing ruled quietly—violence yields to culture; that is Heaven’s rhythm.”

sentences.zh: 」勒大悅。

translations.literal: ” Le was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: ” Shi Le beamed.

sentences.zh: 光因曰：「皇太子仁孝溫恭，中山王雄暴多詐，陛下一旦不諱，臣恐社稷必危，宜漸奪中山威權，使太子早參朝政。

translations.literal: Guang then said, “The crown prince is benevolent, filial, warm, and respectful; the Prince of Zhongshan is fierce, violent, and full of deceit—once Your Majesty passes, your servant fears the altars must be in peril; you ought gradually to strip Zhongshan of awe and authority and let the crown prince early join court government.”
translations.idiomatic: Xu Guang added: “The crown prince is mild; Zhongshan king Shi Hu is brutal—when you die the state may fall; strip Shi Hu’s power and bring the heir into policy now.”

sentences.zh: 」勒納之。

translations.literal: ” Le accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: ” Shi Le listened.

sentences.zh: 程遐又言於勒曰：「中山王勇武權智，群臣莫有及者。

translations.literal: Cheng Xia again spoke to Le: “The Prince of Zhongshan is brave, martial, scheming, and wise—among ministers none reaches him.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Xia warned again: “Shi Hu’s courage and cunning outstrip every minister.

sentences.zh: 觀其志也，自陛下之外，視之蔑如。

translations.literal: Judging his intent, apart from Your Majesty, he views others as worthless.
translations.idiomatic: Except for you he treats all men as dust.

sentences.zh: 兼荷專征歲久，威振外內，性又不仁，殘忍無賴。

translations.literal: Moreover he has long borne sole expedition command, his might shakes inner and outer, and his nature is moreover not benevolent—cruel, ruthless, and without scruple.
translations.idiomatic: He has held independent command for years, tyrannizes court and camp, and knows no mercy.

sentences.zh: 其諸子並長，皆預兵權。

translations.literal: His sons are all grown and each shares military authority.
translations.idiomatic: His grown sons all hold troops.

sentences.zh: 陛下在，自當無他，恐其怏怏不可輔少主也。

translations.literal: While Your Majesty is alive, naturally there will be nothing else to fear; I fear his sullenness will make him unable to assist a young lord.
translations.idiomatic: While you live he behaves—but I doubt he will serve a boy emperor willingly.

sentences.zh: 宜早除之，以便大計。

translations.literal: You ought early to remove him to smooth the great plan.
translations.idiomatic: Remove him now for the dynasty’s sake.

sentences.zh: 」勒曰：「今天下未平，兵難未已，大雅沖幼，宜任強輔。

translations.literal: ” Le said, “The realm is not yet settled, military disaster is not yet ended; Daya is young and tender—it is fitting to employ a strong assistant.
translations.idiomatic: ” Shi Le answered: “The realm is still at war; Daya needs a strong arm.

sentences.zh: 中山佐命功臣，親同魯衛，方委以伊霍之任，何至如卿言也。

translations.literal: The Prince of Zhongshan is a meritorious minister who aided the mandate, close as Lu and Wei—I am about to entrust him with Yi and Huo’s charge—how could it reach what you say?
translations.idiomatic: Zhongshan is a founding pillar, kin as close as Lu and Wei; I mean to make him regent like Yi Yin or Huo Guang—why your panic?

sentences.zh: 卿當恐輔幼主之日，不得獨擅帝舅之權故耳。

translations.literal: You must fear that on the day you assist the young lord you will not get alone to monopolize the power of the imperial maternal uncle—that is all.
translations.idiomatic: You only fear losing your monopoly as the empress’s uncle once a regency begins.

sentences.zh: 吾亦當參卿于顧命，勿為過懼也。

translations.literal: I shall also include you in the testamentary charge—do not be overly fearful.”
translations.idiomatic: I will name you to the testament too—do not dread so much.”

sentences.zh: 」遐泣曰：「臣所言者至公，陛下以私賜距，豈明主開襟納說，忠臣必盡之義乎！

translations.literal: ” Xia wept and said, “What your servant speaks is utmost public-mindedness; Your Majesty rejects it with private favor—how is this an enlightened lord’s open bosom to accept speech and a loyal minister’s duty to exhaust words!
translations.idiomatic: ” Cheng Xia wept: “I speak for the state; you dismiss me as jealous—where is the ruler who hears truth?”

sentences.zh: 中山雖為皇太后所養，非陛下天屬，不可以親義期也。

translations.literal: Although Zhongshan was reared by the empress dowager, he is not Your Majesty’s flesh—one cannot expect him with bonds of kinship.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu was raised by the empress dowager but is not your blood—do not trust kinship.

sentences.zh: 杖陛下神規，微建鷹犬之效，陛下酬其父子以恩榮，亦以足矣。

translations.literal: Relying on Your Majesty’s divine plan, he in small part built hawk-and-hound service; Your Majesty has repaid his father and son with favor and glory—already that is enough.
translations.idiomatic: He earned favor as your hound; you have paid his house enough.

sentences.zh: 魏任司馬懿父子，終於鼎祚淪移，以此而觀，中山豈將來有益者乎！

translations.literal: Wei employed Sima Yi and his son—at last the cauldron fortune shifted; viewing by this, can Zhongshan in the future be one who brings benefit!
translations.idiomatic: Wei trusted the Simas and lost the throne—how can Shi Hu benefit your line?

sentences.zh: 臣因緣多幸，托瓜葛於東宮，臣而不竭言于陛下，而誰言之！

translations.literal: Your servant, by many fortunate ties, has attached himself by marriage to the Eastern Palace; if your servant does not exhaust words to Your Majesty, who will speak them!
translations.idiomatic: I am tied to the heir by marriage—if I stay silent, who warns you?”

sentences.zh: 陛下若不除中山，臣已見社稷不復血食矣。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty does not remove the Prince of Zhongshan, your servant already sees that the altars will not again receive blood offerings.”
translations.idiomatic: “Unless you cut down Shi Hu, I see the dynasty’s sacrifices ending.”

sentences.zh: 」勒不聽。

translations.literal: ” Le would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: ” Shi Le ignored him.

sentences.zh: 遐退告徐光曰：「主上向言如此，太子必危，將若之何？

translations.literal: Xia withdrew and told Xu Guang, “The sovereign’s words just now being so, the crown prince must be in peril—what is to be done?
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Xia told Xu Guang: “The way he brushed you off dooms the crown prince—what now?”

sentences.zh: 」光曰：「中山常切齒於吾二人，恐非但國危，亦為家禍，當為安國甯家之計，不可坐而受禍也。

translations.literal: ” Guang said, “The Prince of Zhongshan constantly grinds his teeth at us two—your servant fears not only the state’s peril but also a family calamity; we ought to plan to secure the state and quiet the family—we cannot sit and receive disaster.”
translations.idiomatic: ” Xu Guang answered: “Shi Hu hates us both; we must save the state and our skins—we cannot sit still.”

sentences.zh: 」光復承間言於勒曰：「陛下廓平八州，帝有海內，而神色不悅者何也？

translations.literal: ” Guang again seized an occasion to say to Le, “Your Majesty has widened and pacified eight provinces and imperially possesses within the seas—why is your expression not pleased?”
translations.idiomatic: ” Xu Guang tried again: “You rule eight provinces—why the long face?”

sentences.zh: 」勒曰：「吳、蜀未平，書軌不一，司馬家猶不絕於丹陽，恐後之人將以吾為不應符錄，每一思之，不覺見於神色。

translations.literal: ” Le said, “Wu and Shu are not yet settled, writing and tracks are not one, and the Sima house is still not cut off at Danyang—your servant fears later men will say I did not match the talisman registers; each time I think of it, it cannot help showing in my expression.”
translations.idiomatic: ” Shi Le said: “Wu and Shu remain, the Simas still hold the south—I fear history will say I lacked the mandate; it shows on my face.”

sentences.zh: 」光曰：「臣以陛下為憂腹心之患，而何暇更憂四支手！

translations.literal: ” Guang said, “Your servant thought Your Majesty worried a heart-and-belly trouble—why spare care for the four limbs!”
translations.idiomatic: ” Xu Guang replied: “I thought you feared a gut wound—why worry about scratched fingers?”

sentences.zh: 何則？

translations.literal: How so?
translations.idiomatic: What do you mean?

sentences.zh: 魏承漢運，為正朔帝王，劉備雖紹興巴、蜀，亦不可謂漢不滅也。

translations.literal: Wei inherited Han’s fortune as orthodox Son of Heaven; though Liu Bei continued the line in Ba and Shu, still one cannot say Han did not perish.
translations.idiomatic: Wei succeeded Han as the true line; Liu Bei’s Shu did not keep Han alive.

sentences.zh: 吳雖跨江東，豈有虧魏美？

translations.literal: Though Wu straddled east of the River, how could it diminish Wei’s excellence?
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Wu never disproved Wei’s legitimacy.

sentences.zh: 陛下既苞括二都，為中國帝王，彼司馬家兒復何異玄德，李氏亦猶孫權。

translations.literal: Your Majesty already embraces the two capitals and is Son of Heaven of the Central Lands—how do those Sima boys differ from Xuande, and the Li clan is likewise like Sun Quan.
translations.idiomatic: You hold both capitals—southern Simas are no more than Liu Bei, and Li Xiong is another Sun Quan.

sentences.zh: 符籙不在陛下，竟欲安歸？

translations.literal: If the talisman registers are not with Your Majesty, where in the end could they wish to go?
translations.idiomatic: If the mandate is not yours, whose can it be?

sentences.zh: 此四支之輕患耳。

translations.literal: These are light troubles of the four limbs.”
translations.idiomatic: They are only limb aches.”

sentences.zh: 中山王藉陛下指授神略，天下皆言其英武亞于陛下，兼其殘暴多奸，見利忘義，無伊、霍之忠。

translations.literal: The Prince of Zhongshan, relying on Your Majesty’s finger-pointed divine strategy, is said by all under Heaven to be next only to Your Majesty in heroic martialness, and moreover he is cruel, violent, and full of deceit, seeing profit and forgetting righteousness, without Yi or Huo’s loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu, riding your prestige, passes for second only to you—yet he is treacherous, cruel, and no Yi Yin.

sentences.zh: 父子爵位之重，勢傾王室。

translations.literal: Father and son’s noble rank’s weight makes their power tilt the royal house.
translations.idiomatic: Father and son hold such titles they overshadow the throne.

sentences.zh: 觀其耿耿，常有不滿之心。

translations.literal: Observing his uneasy glare, he constantly has a heart of discontent.
translations.idiomatic: His smoldering looks show discontent.

sentences.zh: 近于東宮曲宴，有輕皇太子之色。

translations.literal: Lately at a bent banquet in the Eastern Palace he showed belittling color toward the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: At a recent heir’s banquet he openly sneered at the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 陛下隱忍容之，臣恐陛下萬年之後，宗廟必生荊刺，此心腹之重疾也，惟陛下圖之。

translations.literal: Your Majesty secretly bears and tolerates him—your servant fears that after Your Majesty’s myriad years, thorns will surely grow in the ancestral temple; this is a grave illness of heart and belly—only may Your Majesty plan for it.”
translations.idiomatic: You indulge him—after your death the temple will sprout thorns; this is the cancer to cure.”

sentences.zh: 」勒默然，而竟不從。

translations.literal: ” Le was silent, yet in the end did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: ” Shi Le stayed silent and did nothing.

sentences.zh: 及勒死，季龍執弘使臨軒，命收程遐、徐光下廷尉，召其子邃率兵入宿衛，文武靡不奔散。

translations.literal: When Le died, Tigun seized Hong, made him face the hall, ordered Cheng Xia and Xu Guang seized and sent down to the commandant of justice, summoned his son Sui to lead troops into palace guard duty, and civil and military all fled in scatter.
translations.idiomatic: At Shi Le’s death Shi Hu seized Shi Hong at audience, jailed Cheng Xia and Xu Guang, called Shi Sui’s troops into the palace, and the court scattered.

sentences.zh: 弘大懼，讓位于季龍。

translations.literal: Hong was greatly frightened and ceded position to Tigun.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hong, terrified, offered Shi Hu the throne.

sentences.zh: 季龍曰：「君薨而世子立，臣安敢亂之！

translations.literal: Tigun said, “When the lord dies and the heir apparent is set—how dare a minister throw it into chaos!”
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu refused: “The heir succeeds the father—how could I usurp?”

sentences.zh: 」弘泣而固讓，季龍怒曰：「若其不堪，天下自當有大議，何足預論！

translations.literal: ” Hong wept and firmly ceded; Tigun angrily said, “If he is not adequate, the realm itself will have a great debate—what need to discuss it beforehand!”
translations.idiomatic: ” When Shi Hong wept and insisted, Shi Hu snarled that unfit rulers fall by public verdict—no need to debate now.”

sentences.zh: 」遂以咸和七年逼立之，改年曰延熙，文武百僚進位一等。

translations.literal: ” Thereupon in the seventh year of Xianhe he compelled him to consent, changed the era name to Yanxi, and civil and military hundred officials each advanced one rank.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianhe 7 he forced Shi Hong’s compliance, renamed the era Yanxi, and promoted every official one step.

sentences.zh: 誅程遐、徐光。

translations.literal: He executed Cheng Xia and Xu Guang.
translations.idiomatic: He killed Cheng Xia and Xu Guang.

sentences.zh: 弘策拜季龍為丞相、魏王、大單于，加九錫，以魏郡等十三郡為邑，總攝百揆。

translations.literal: Hong ceremonially appointed Tigun chancellor, Prince of Wei, Grand Chanyu, adding the nine bestowals, with Wei commandery and thirteen other commanderies as fief, overall holding the hundred handles.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hong named Shi Hu chancellor, prince of Wei, grand Chanyu, with the nine insignia and thirteen commanderies as fief, running the whole administration.

sentences.zh: 季龍偽固讓，久而受命，赦其境內殊死已下，立季龍妻鄭氏為魏王后，子邃為魏太子，加使持節、侍中、大都督中外諸軍事、大將軍、錄尚書事；

translations.literal: Tigun falsely declined for a long time, then accepted the mandate, amnestied capital crimes and below within his borders, established Tigun’s wife Lady Zheng as Wei queen, son Sui as Wei heir apparent, adding bearer of credentials, palace attendant, grand supervisor of all military affairs of inner and outer, grand general, recorder of masters-of-writing affairs;
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu feigned refusal, then took power, amnestied capital crimes, made Lady Zheng queen of Wei, Shi Sui heir of Wei with full military and secretariat portfolios;

sentences.zh: 宣為使持節、車騎大將軍、冀州刺史，封河間王；

translations.literal: Xuan as bearer of credentials, grand general of chariots and cavalry, Inspector of Ji, enfeoffed Prince of Hejian;
translations.idiomatic: Shi Xuan became chariot-cavalry general and prince of Hejian with Ji province;

sentences.zh: 韜為前鋒將軍、司隸校尉，封樂安王；

translations.literal: Tao as vanguard general, colonel-director of the retainers, enfeoffed Prince of Le’an;
translations.idiomatic: Shi Tao became vanguard general, metropolitan commandant, prince of Le’an;

sentences.zh: 遵齊王，鑒代王，苞樂平王；

translations.literal: Zun Prince of Qi, Jian Prince of Dai, Bao Prince of Leping;
translations.idiomatic: Shi Zun prince of Qi, Shi Jian prince of Dai, Shi Bao prince of Leping;

sentences.zh: 徙太原王斌為章武王。

translations.literal: he moved Prince of Taiyuan Bin to be Prince of Zhangwu.
translations.idiomatic: he transferred Taiyuan prince Shi Bin to Zhangwu.

sentences.zh: 勒文武舊臣皆補左右丞相閑任，季龍府僚舊昵悉署台省禁要。

translations.literal: Le’s old civil and military ministers were all given idle posts as left and right chancellors; Tigun’s house clerks and old intimates were all assigned to terrace and palace key posts.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le’s old guard got sinceure chancellorships while Shi Hu’s cronies took the real ministries.

sentences.zh: 命太子宮曰崇訓宮，勒妻劉氏已下皆居之。

translations.literal: He ordered the crown prince’s palace titled Exalted Instruction Palace, and Le’s wife Lady Liu downward all dwelt there.
translations.idiomatic: He renamed the heir’s palace “Exalted Instruction” and moved Lady Liu and Le’s harem inside.

sentences.zh: 簡其美淑及勒車馬、珍寶、服御之上者，皆入於己署。

translations.literal: He selected their beauties and the best of Le’s carriages, horses, treasures, and wardrobe and took them into his own offices.
translations.idiomatic: He cherry-picked Le’s women, chariots, and treasures for himself.

sentences.zh: 鎮軍夔安領左僕射，尚書郭殷為右僕射。

translations.literal: Army Guard Kui An headed the left supervisor of the masters of writing, Master of Writing Guo Yin the right supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: Kui An became left secretariat director, Guo Yin right director.

sentences.zh: 劉氏謂石堪曰：「皇祚之滅不復久矣，王將何以圖之？

translations.literal: Lady Liu said to Shi Kan, “The imperial fortune’s extinction will not again be long—how will the prince plan for it?”
translations.idiomatic: Lady Liu told Shi Kan: “The house is doomed—what will you do?”

sentences.zh: 」堪曰：「先帝舊臣皆已斥外，眾旅不復由人，宮殿之內無所措籌，臣請出奔袞州，據廩丘，挾南陽王為盟主，宣太后詔于諸牧守征鎮，令各率義兵同討桀逆，蔑不濟也。

translations.literal: ” Kan said, “The late emperor’s old ministers have all been cast outside; hosts of troops are no longer at men’s disposal; within the palace there is nowhere to plot—your servant asks to flee to Yanzhou, hold Linyi, take the Prince of Nanyang as covenant lord, proclaim the empress dowager’s edict to shepherds and garrison commanders, and order each to lead righteous troops jointly to punish the fierce rebel—nothing will not succeed.”
translations.idiomatic: ” Shi Kan proposed fleeing to Yanzhou, rallying at Linyi behind the Prince of Nanyang, and issuing the empress’s call for loyal troops against Shi Hu.”

sentences.zh: 」劉氏曰：「事急矣，便可速發，恐事淹變生。

translations.literal: ” Lady Liu said, “The affair is urgent—at once you may hasten to set out; your servant fears delay will breed change.”
translations.idiomatic: ” Lady Liu said: “Move tonight—delay invites betrayal.”

sentences.zh: 」堪許諾，微服輕騎襲袞州，失期，不克，遂南奔譙城。

translations.literal: Kan promised, changed clothes, and with light horse raided Yanzhou; he missed the date, did not take it, and thereupon fled south to Qiao city.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Kan slipped out in disguise, failed to seize Yanzhou, and ran toward Qiao.

sentences.zh: 季龍遣其將郭太等追擊之，獲堪于城父，送襄國，炙而殺之。

translations.literal: Tigun sent his general Guo Tai and others in pursuit, captured Kan at Chengfu, sent him to Xiangguo, and roasted him alive to death.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu’s Guo Tai ran him down at Chengfu, brought him to Xiangguo, and roasted him alive.

sentences.zh: 征石恢還于襄國。

translations.literal: He summoned Shi Hui back to Xiangguo.
translations.idiomatic: He recalled Shi Hui to Xiangguo.

sentences.zh: 劉氏謀泄，季龍殺之。

translations.literal: Lady Liu’s plot leaked; Tigun killed her.
translations.idiomatic: When Lady Liu’s plot leaked, Shi Hu killed her.

sentences.zh: 尊弘母程氏為皇太后。

translations.literal: He honored Hong’s mother Lady Cheng as empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: He named Shi Hong’s mother Cheng empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 時石生鎮關中，石朗鎮洛陽，皆起兵於二鎮。

translations.literal: At the time Shi Sheng held Guanzhong and Shi Lang held Luoyang; both raised troops at the two garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Sheng in Guanzhong and Shi Lang in Luoyang rose simultaneously.

sentences.zh: 季龍留子邃守襄國，統步騎七萬攻郎于金墉。

translations.literal: Tigun left his son Sui to guard Xiangguo and commanded seventy thousand foot and horse to attack Lang at Jinyong.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu left Shi Sui in Xiangguo and marched seventy thousand men on Shi Lang at Jinyong.

sentences.zh: 金墉潰，獲朗，刖而斬之。

translations.literal: Jinyong collapsed; he captured Lang, cut off his feet, then beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Jinyong fell; Shi Hu mutilated Shi Lang and then beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 進師攻長安，以石挺為前鋒大都督。

translations.literal: He advanced the army to attack Chang’an, making Shi Ting grand vanguard commander.
translations.idiomatic: He drove on Chang’an with Shi Ting as grand vanguard.

sentences.zh: 生遣將軍郭權率鮮卑涉璝部眾二萬為前鋒距之，生統大軍繼發，次於蒲阪。

translations.literal: Sheng sent General Guo Quan to lead twenty thousand of the Xianbei Shegui tribe’s host as vanguard to oppose him; Sheng commanded the great army afterward, halting at Puyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Sheng sent Guo Quan with twenty thousand Shegui Xianbei as van while he followed to Puyuan.

sentences.zh: 前鋒及挺大戰潼關，敗績，挺及丞相左長史劉隗皆戰死，季龍退奔澠池，枕屍三百餘里。

translations.literal: The vanguard and Ting fought a great battle at Tong Pass and were routed; Ting and the chancellor’s left chief clerk Liu Wei both died in battle; Tigun retreated fleeing to Mianchi, corpses pillowing the ground for over three hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: The van clashed with Shi Ting at Tong Pass and broke; Shi Ting and Liu Wei died; Shi Hu fled to Mianchi over three hundred li of corpses.

sentences.zh: 鮮卑密通于季龍，背生而擊之。

translations.literal: The Xianbei secretly communicated with Tigun, turned their backs on Sheng, and struck him.
translations.idiomatic: The Xianbei defected to Shi Hu and hit Shi Sheng from behind.

sentences.zh: 生時停蒲阪，不知挺之死也，懼，單馬奔長安。

translations.literal: Sheng at the time was halted at Puyuan and did not know of Ting’s death; he feared, and on a single horse fled to Chang’an.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Sheng, still at Puyuan and unaware Shi Ting was dead, panicked and galloped alone to Chang’an.

sentences.zh: 郭權乃復收眾三千，與越騎校尉石廣相持於渭汭。

translations.literal: Guo Quan thereupon again gathered a host of three thousand and with Colonel of the Yueqiang Shi Guang faced each other at the Wei’s bend.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Quan rallied three thousand men and stalled Shi Guang at the Wei ford.

sentences.zh: 生遂去長安，潛於雞頭山。

translations.literal: Sheng thereupon left Chang’an and hid on Chicken Head Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Sheng abandoned Chang’an for Chicken Head Mountain.

sentences.zh: 將軍蔣英固守長安。

translations.literal: General Jiang Ying stoutly held Chang’an.
translations.idiomatic: General Jiang Ying held Chang’an.

sentences.zh: 季龍聞生之奔也，進師入關，進攻長安，旬餘拔之，斬蔣英等。

translations.literal: Tigun, hearing of Sheng’s flight, advanced the army into the passes, attacked Chang’an, took it in a bit over ten days, and beheaded Jiang Ying and others.
translations.idiomatic: Learning Shi Sheng had fled, Shi Hu stormed Chang’an, took it in ten days, and killed Jiang Ying.

sentences.zh: 分遣諸將屯於汧。

translations.literal: He separately sent various generals to encamp at Qian.
translations.idiomatic: He posted generals along the Qian River.

sentences.zh: 徙雍、秦州華戎十餘萬戶於關東。

translations.literal: He moved over one hundred thousand households of Yong and Qinzhou Chinese and barbarians east of the passes.
translations.idiomatic: He deported a hundred thousand Yong and Qin households east of the pass.

sentences.zh: 生部下斬生於雞頭山。

translations.literal: Sheng’s subordinates beheaded Sheng on Chicken Head Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Sheng’s own men beheaded him on Chicken Head Mountain.

sentences.zh: 季龍還襄國，大赦，諷弘命己建魏台，一如魏輔漢故事。

translations.literal: Tigun returned to Xiangguo, granted a great amnesty, and prompted Hong to order him to establish the Wei terrace, entirely like Wei assisting Han’s precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Back in Xiangguo he amnestied the realm and made Shi Hong charter a Wei-style advisory terrace like Cao Cao’s.

sentences.zh: 郭權以生敗，據上邽以歸順，詔以權為鎮西將軍、秦州刺史，於是京兆、新平、扶風、馮翊、北地皆應之。

translations.literal: Guo Quan, because Sheng was defeated, held Shanggui to submit to allegiance; an edict appointed Quan General Who Guards the West and Inspector of Qinzhou, whereupon Jingzhao, Xinping, Fufeng, Fengyi, and Beidi all responded to him.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Quan held Shanggui for the court and was named western guardian and Qinzhou inspector; five commanderies rallied to him.

sentences.zh: 弘鎮西石廣與權戰，敗績。

translations.literal: Hong’s western-area commander Shi Guang fought Quan and was routed.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hong’s western commander Shi Guang lost to Guo Quan.

sentences.zh: 季龍遣郭敖及其子斌等率步騎四萬討之，次於華陰。

translations.literal: Tigun sent Guo Ao and his son Bin and others to lead forty thousand foot and horse to punish him, halting at Huayin.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu sent Guo Ao and Shi Bin with forty thousand troops to Huayin.

sentences.zh: 上邽豪族害權以降。

translations.literal: Shanggui’s powerful clans killed Quan to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Shanggui magnates murdered Guo Quan and capitulated.

sentences.zh: 徙秦州三萬餘戶於青、並二州諸郡。

translations.literal: He moved over thirty thousand households of Qinzhou to various commanderies of Qing and Bing provinces.
translations.idiomatic: He resettled thirty thousand Qinzhou households into Qing and Bing.

sentences.zh: 南氐、楊難敵等送任通和。

translations.literal: Southern Di and Yang Nandi and others sent hostages to open peace.
translations.idiomatic: Southern Di chiefs including Yang Nandi sent hostages for peace.

sentences.zh: 長安陳良夫奔于黑羌，招誘北羌四角王薄句大等擾北地、馮翊，與石斌相持。

translations.literal: Chang’an’s Chen Liangfu fled to the Black Qiang, enticed and summoned the northern Qiang four-corner king Bo Judda and others to disturb Beidi and Fengyi, facing Shi Bin in stalemate.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Liangfu of Chang’an fled to Black Qiang, roused chief Bo Judda to raid Beidi and Fengyi, and stalled Shi Bin.

sentences.zh: 石韜等率騎掎句大之後，與斌夾擊，敗之，句大奔於馬蘭山。

translations.literal: Shi Tao and others led horse to pinch Judda’s rear, jointly striking with Bin, defeated him, and Judda fled to Malan Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Tao rode behind Bo Judda while Shi Bin struck frontally; the chief fled to Malan Mountain.

sentences.zh: 郭敖等懸軍追北，為羌所敗，死者十七八。

translations.literal: Guo Ao and others, with army suspended, pursued north, were defeated by Qiang, and seven or eight in ten died.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ao’s pursuit column was ambushed by Qiang and lost eight men in ten.

sentences.zh: 斌等收軍還於三城。

translations.literal: Bin and others gathered the army and returned to Three Cities.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Bin rallied the survivors back to Sancheng.

sentences.zh: 季龍聞而大怒，遣使殺郭敖。

translations.literal: Tigun heard and was greatly angry, sent envoys to kill Guo Ao.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu, furious, had Guo Ao executed by messenger.

sentences.zh: 石宏有怒言，季龍幽之。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qin Shi Hong had angry words; Tigun imprisoned him.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qin, another clansman also named Shi Hong, muttered threats, so Shi Hu jailed him.

sentences.zh: 弘齎璽綬親詣季龍，諭禪位意。

translations.literal: Hong carried the jade and ribbon in person to visit Tigun, explaining intent to yield the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hong brought the imperial seals to Shi Hu and offered abdication.

sentences.zh: 季龍曰：「天下人自當有議，何為自論此也！

translations.literal: Tigun said, “Men of the realm will themselves have a discussion—why raise this on your own!”
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu said: “The realm will judge succession—do not speak of yielding!”

sentences.zh: 」弘還宮，對其母流涕曰：「先帝真無復遺矣！

translations.literal: ” Hong returned to the palace, wept to his mother, and said, “The late emperor truly left nothing further!”
translations.idiomatic: ” Back in the palace Shi Hong wept to his mother that his father had left him defenseless.

sentences.zh: 」俄而季龍遣丞相郭殷持節入，廢弘為海陽王。

translations.literal: ” Soon Tigun sent Chancellor Guo Yin bearing credentials within, deposed Hong as Prince of Haiyang.
translations.idiomatic: ” Soon Shi Hu’s Guo Yin entered with credentials and demoted Shi Hong to prince of Haiyang.

sentences.zh: 弘安步就車，容色自若，謂群臣曰：「不堪纂承大統，顧慚群後，此亦天命去矣，又何言！

translations.literal: Hong calmly walked to the carriage, his bearing and color self-possessed, and said to the host of ministers, “Unable to succeed to the great line, I am ashamed before the regional lords—this too is Heaven’s mandate departing—what more is there to say!”
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hong walked to his coach composed, telling the court he was unfit, ashamed before the lords, and yielding to fate.

sentences.zh: 」百官莫不流涕，宮人慟哭。

translations.literal: The hundred officials none did not weep tears; palace women wailed in grief.
translations.idiomatic: Officials wept; palace women howled.

sentences.zh: 咸康元年，幽弘及程氏並宏、恢于崇訓宮，尋殺之，在位二年，時年二十二。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xiankang he imprisoned Shi Hong the emperor, Lady Cheng, together with the Prince of Qin Shi Hong and Shi Hui in Exalted Instruction Palace, soon killed them; Shi Hong had occupied the throne two years, age twenty-two.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiankang 1 Shi Hu caged Emperor Shi Hong, Lady Cheng, the Prince of Qin Shi Hong, and Shi Hui in Exalted Instruction Palace and soon murdered them; the emperor had reigned two years and died at twenty-two.

sentences.zh: 張賓，字孟孫，趙郡中丘人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Bin, style Mengsun, was a man of Zhongqiu in Zhao commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Bin, courtesy Mengsun, came from Zhongqiu in Zhao.

sentences.zh: 父瑤，中山太守。

translations.literal: His father Yao was Administrator of Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhang Yao governed Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 賓少好學，博涉經史，不為章句，闊達有大節，常謂昆弟曰：「吾自言智算鑒識不後子房，但不遇高祖耳。

translations.literal: Bin in youth loved learning, broadly traversed classics and histories, did not do chapter-and-phrase studies, was open and had great integrity, and often told his brothers, “I myself say that in wisdom, calculation, insight, and judgment I do not lag behind Zifang—I only have not met the Exalted Founder.”
translations.idiomatic: He read widely, scorned pedantic glossing, and told his brothers he matched Zhang Liang in wit—only lacking a Liu Bang.

sentences.zh: 」為中丘王帳下都督，非其好也，病免。

translations.literal: ” He was camp colonel under the Prince of Zhongqiu—not his liking—and retired on illness.
translations.idiomatic: ” He served the prince of Zhongqiu as camp colonel, disliked it, and quit on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 及永嘉大亂，石勒為劉元海輔漢將軍，與諸將下山東，賓謂所親曰：「吾曆觀諸將多矣，獨胡將軍可與共成大事。

translations.literal: When the Yongjia great chaos came, Shi Le was Liu Yuanhai’s General Who Supports Han and with the generals went down to east of the mountains; Bin told those close, “Your servant has surveyed the many generals—only General Hu can with him complete a great enterprise.”
translations.idiomatic: When chaos erupted, Shi Le was Liu Yuan’s assistant general invading Shandong; Zhang Bin told friends only the “Hu general” could build an empire.

sentences.zh: 」乃提劍軍門，大呼請見，勒亦未之奇也。

translations.literal: ” Then he lifted his sword at the army gate, shouted loudly asking audience; Le also did not yet think him extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: ” He drew his sword at Shi Le’s gate and demanded an audience; Shi Le saw nothing special yet.

sentences.zh: 後漸進規謨，乃異之，引為謀主。

translations.literal: Later, as he gradually advanced plans and counsels, Le marveled at him and drew him in as chief strategist.
translations.idiomatic: As his stratagems piled up, Shi Le made him chief planner.

sentences.zh: 機不虛發，算無遺策，成勒之基業，皆賓之勳也。

translations.literal: Opportunity never issued in vain; calculation left no strategy behind; completing Le’s foundation enterprise was all Bin’s merit.
translations.idiomatic: His plots never misfired; every Shi Le victory owed Zhang Bin.

sentences.zh: 及為右長史、大執法，封濮陽侯，任遇優顯，寵冠當時，而謙虛敬慎，開襟下士，士無賢愚，造之者莫不得盡其情焉。

translations.literal: When he became right chief clerk and grand judicial overseer, enfeoffed Marquis of Puyang, his commission and favor were eminent and his grace topped the age, yet he was humble, respectful, and cautious, opening his bosom to humble scholars—whether shi were worthy or foolish, none who visited him failed to obtain full expression of their feelings.
translations.idiomatic: As right chief clerk, grand law officer, and marquis of Puyang he stood highest at court yet stayed modest, heard every petitioner out, wise or dull.

sentences.zh: 肅清百僚，屏絕私昵，入則格言，出則歸美。

translations.literal: He purified the hundred officials, screened off private favoritism; entering he offered model words, exiting he returned credit to others’ beauty.
translations.idiomatic: He cleansed the bureaucracy of cliques, spoke truth in council, and credited others outside it.

sentences.zh: 勒甚重之，每朝，常為之正容貌，簡辭令，呼曰「右侯」而不名之，勒朝莫與為比也。

translations.literal: Le greatly valued him; each court session he regularly for Bin straightened bearing and simplified wording, calling him “Lord of the Right” without speaking his name; in Le’s court none could compare with him.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le tidied his dress before every audience with Zhang Bin, called him “Lord Right” instead of his name, and favored him above all.

sentences.zh: 及卒，勒親臨哭之，哀慟左右，贈散騎常侍、右光祿大夫、儀同三司，諡曰景。

translations.literal: When he died, Le personally attended and wept for him, grieving so that those to left and right were moved, posthumously bestowing cavalier attendant-in-ordinary, right grand master of splendid brightness, and three offices with equal ceremonial, posthumous title Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le mourned at his bier, showered posthumous honors, and gave him the posthumous name Jing (“bright”).

sentences.zh: 將葬，送于正陽門，望之流涕，顧左右曰：「天欲不成吾事邪，何奪吾右侯之早也！

translations.literal: When about to bury him, he escorted to Zhengyang Gate, gazed on him and shed tears, turned to those at his side and said, “Does Heaven wish not to complete my enterprise—why take my Lord of the Right so early!”
translations.idiomatic: At the Zhengyang gate funeral he wept, “Heaven steals my right hand too soon!”

sentences.zh: 」程遐代為右長史，勒每與遐議，有所不合，輒歎曰：「右侯舍我去，令我與此輩共事，豈非酷乎！

translations.literal: ” Cheng Xia replaced him as right chief clerk; each time Le deliberated with Xia and there was disagreement, he would sigh and say, “The Lord of the Right has left me—making me work with this crowd—is it not cruel!”
translations.idiomatic: ” Cheng Xia succeeded him; whenever Shi Le argued with Cheng Xia he groaned, “Right Lord gone—I must endure these mediocrities—cruel fate!”

translations.literal: ” Thereupon he wept flowing tears a whole day.
translations.idiomatic: ” And he wept all day.
